Latest Update: Man United Confidential: Mauricio Pochettino to be given money to spend in January as club target recruits in THREE positions - and surprise at popular coach's sacking

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s latest head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s latest head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.

Pochettino will leave the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati after the USA’s game against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning and go straight to the airport to catch an eight-hour flight to Manchester on board a private jet paid for by United.

The club will also provide him with somewhere to live as he settles into the latest job and finds a more permanent residence.

The 54-year-old, who also has a home in Barcelona, is stated to have lived just outside London when he was Tottenham manager and then spent the entirety of his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain boss in a luxury hotel.

Pochettino lived in Knightsbridge while he was in charge of Chelsea, and revealed that he enjoyed getting feedback from fans while out on his daily 90-minute dog walks with Sansa.

He named the Rhodesian Ridgeback after a character from Game of Thrones and has even given the dog her own Instagram account.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the US national team for the final time in the early hours of Wednesday morning, then head straight to Manchester on a private jet.

Pochettino (pictured with his son Maurizio) will have to find accommodation which suits his dog Sansa, a Rhodesian Ridgeback (Source: Instagram/pochettino).

Describing the difficulty of Spurs playing on a Saturday night in 2018, he mentioned: ‘At 7pm, I am normally on my sofa with my dog Sansa watching the Spanish league because they start at 7.45pm, or France because Ligue 1 starts at 8pm, or Italy, or different games.

Industry observers note that ‘It will be so strange for my dog. Not for me but my dog. “Where is my dad?” she is going to say. She is beautiful and I am in love with her.’.

Sources indicate that the living habits of United bosses have varied over the years. Sir Alex Ferguson, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim favoured Wilmslow and Alderley Edge, David Moyes remained further afield in Lytham, Louis van Gaal and Erik ten Hag chose Hale, and Jose Mourinho famously spent 895 days at the Lowry Hotel in Manchester (where dogs can stay for an additional £30).

United have no aims to change the timings for Wednesday’s training session, even though Pochettino and four of his backroom team may not arrive at Carrington until the early afternoon.

The private jet carrying the Argentine, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott should touch down from Cincinnati around noon.

An advance party of three more coaches – Pochettino’s assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have been in Manchester since Sunday after they were released early by the US Soccer Federation as a gesture of goodwill following the 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti in the quarter-finals of the North American equivalent of the Nations League.

They took training on Tuesday as United’s players continue to report back from international duty, and will also oversee the session on Wednesday morning after United decided not to reschedule it so Pochettino could be present.

The Argentine will be firmly hands-on from Thursday, though, as he prepares for his first game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino, who will speak to club media shortly after his arrival before conducting his first press conference on Friday, has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez (right) has been in Manchester since Sunday and took training on Tuesday.

Strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya - the first woman to be part of United's backroom staff - will travel with Pochettino to Manchester following the Haiti game.

Pochettino will inherit a team in the relegation zone – which could even be bottom of the Premier League by kick-off on Sunday – and it’s understood he will be given modest funds to improve his squad in the January transfer window.

United are in desperate need of a left back and a striker, having failed to sign cover in both positions in the summer.

One potential target may be US centre forward Folarin Balogun who has prospered under Pochettino but only started once for Monaco this season after a summer move to Everton fell through. United sources say the latest head coach will have input in the weeks ahead before a clearer plan emerges.

United also want a centre back after Confidential revealed last week that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins, of Brentford, are two options being considered.

It’s possible that one of those deals may have to be a loan, however, with United’s delicate financial situation set to be spelt out in black and white when the results from the first quarter of the financial year are released on Thursday.

Although Pochettino is going to have money for latest players, United will have to be smart in their transfer dealings and spend wisely.

In the short term, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford may be available again for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

However, there is a concern over Patrick Dorgu who was deemed to be unfit for international duty with Denmark, even though he returned to action for Michael Carrick’s final game after a month-and-a-half out with a hamstring injury and headed a stoppage-time equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey (right) is among the centre-back options United are considering.

Marcus Rashford may be available for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

It was the departure of Travis Binnion, rather than Carrick, that raised the most eyebrows among figures working in football over the past few days.

Agents and first-team players privately described their surprise at seeing Binnion – a long-time academy figure before stepping up to the first team to help Darren Fletcher as interim and then Carrick – leave the club.

United have cleaned house for the arrival of Pochettino’s backroom team, and Binnion was one of those who paid the price.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who are known to have enjoyed working with Binnion.

Despite stepping up to the first team, where he would watch matches from the press box alongside United’s team of analysts, Binnion remained in contact with numerous academy player representatives to ensure their development was progressing as planned.

Binnion, who first arrived in 2019 as an Under 16s coach and progressed to the Under 18s, Under 21s and then head of player development and coaching, isn’t expected to be out of the game for too long though.

Agency sources believe rival Premier League academies will move promptly to recruit him, with Everton seen as one potential landing spot. United’s former academy head Nick Cox is now Everton technical director and has already recruited Dave Hughes and Tom Curtis, who worked under Binnion at United.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who enjoyed working with Travis Binnion (pictured).

Your responses to our 36-man Manchester United squad audit have made for interesting reading over the last week.

Confidential pored over the first-team squad, as well as numerous rising stars in the academy, that Pochettino and his staff will quickly have to run the rule over.

While some of the voting went as expected – your votes demonstrated an overwhelming desire among the fanbase to see Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Shaw and Harry Maguire leave this summer – there were a few surprises.

It has been revealed that many voted for captain Bruno Fernandes, who just recently rejected a second contract extension offer, to be moved on, along with Rashford. Amad Diallo and summer signing Andrey Santos are two who divide opinion, but both made the cut.

Check out the full squad audit HERE to see how others voted and leave your own verdict!

Confidential understands JJ Gabriel’s representatives held fresh talks with Real Madrid at the club’s training ground on Monday as a move to the Santiago Bernabeu edges ever closer.

Now that Gabriel has officially confirmed a partnership with Epic Sports Agency, his agent Ali Barat is leading negotiations and has been at Real’s Valdebebas headquarters along with the 16-year-old and his family.

Gabriel confirmed his departure from the club in an Instagram video on Tuesday night, as he and the Spanish giants hope to get a move over the line.

JJ Gabriel's representatives have held fresh talks with Real Madrid as his move to the Bernabeu edges closer.

Eric Cantona and Sir Alex Ferguson will reunite next month at a special screening of the Frenchman’s latest documentary.

Cantona: Flower of Evil won rave reviews in France and is now heading to the UK, with a one-night-only panel featuring Cantona and Ferguson at Aviva Studios in Manchester on December 7.

According to recent reports, the documentary film digs deeper into how Ferguson channelled Cantona’s brilliance and honed his explosiveness – a trait that had seen him branded ‘unmanageable’ in France. Tickets range from £156 all the way up to £1,000. You can purchase them here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three words from the 5,700 Sheffield Wednesday supporters at Oakwell carried so much meaning – especially with Barnsley wandering around looking lost.

The football fans who turn up on freezing cold nights like Friday's and pay to watch a match they could just as easily see from their sofa or a warm pub indisputably love their clubs, but do not always feeling in tune with them.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Barnsley's appreciated the efforts of their players in a frustrating 2-1 loss and understand the handicaps their coach, Daniel Stendel, is fighting against. But their dissatisfaction with the direction those above are taking the club in was vented outside the ground before kick-off.

They cannot see how their club can get back to where they want it to be without a massive change of direction.

In a recent development, the same was true of Wednesday's fans a year ago as they emerged from the wreckage wrought by Dejphon Chansiri. Although David Storch's takeover brought optimism they were not convinced manager Henrik Pedersen was going in quite the right direction.

His successor, Dave Challinor, is miles from his destination but even if it might have been premature after two league games, "Wednesday are back" was a vote of confidence he can guide them to the right path.

The Owls did not play at anywhere near the level of the team they aspire to be. Jamal Lowe's goals were their only shots on target.

Much has been made of the entertainment levels this season, but a night so cold you could see every breath in a derby mismatched enough that you felt the Owls had much more to lose than gain was not about putting on a show, just coming back into the warm three points better off.

Barry Bannan ran around like a man ten years younger, Liam Cooper marshalled his defence, Lowe played in a wide position that demands a lot of dirty work without forgetting his primary job.

Barnsley refused to accept their fate when Lowe scored his second goal after 14 minutes.

According to recent reports, the trouble is, like Wednesday's players last season, they are just not good enough for the level. Between the boxes they are, but not the bits that decide matches.

Their defending for Lowe's goals – leaving Cooper unmarked at a Bannan corner to head across to Lowe, then standing off the striker as he finished a move which took them from the halfway line to the back of the net in two passes and a shot – was relegation standard.

With the exception of Vimal Yoganathan arriving onto Reyes Cleary's low ball in to halve the deficit after 40 minutes, their final balls and finishes were not much better.

That they are trying their best only highlights their best is not good enough – not by much in most games, but by enough in almost all of them. Their winless run in League One now stretches to double figures – unlike their points tally.

Bromley's win at Reading on Saturday sent them bottom of the table.

It is hard to see them escaping relegation without a really good January transfer window, and very hard to imagine even a quite good one.

"When you play games like Sheffield or Stockport or Oxford. Luton, you do not have the feeling the gap is too so massive," noted Stendel after 90 minutes which backed him up.

"Between both boxes, we are surely a team who shouldn't be in the bottom of the league, but games decided not between the boxes.

"You would think, 'What you do in training?' but (on Thursday) we prepared the team especially for a situation like (the second goal).".

Whilst adamant his team can pull things around, Patrick Kelly – standing in for the suspended Cameron McGeehan as captain – was not pulling any punches.

"You can't start games like that," he noted. "We just had too many times this season where we just gave ourselves too much to do.

"We've conceded far too many from free-kicks and stuff.

"After that we were good, probably the better team for the rest of the game, but didn't create enough clear-cut chances.".

Barnsley's doom and gloom was in contrast to the joy of away fans who made up about a third of the crowd condensed into one end.

It felt crucial they shared it with the players at full-time.

In a recent development, "They have to enjoy it and look forward to the next one," noted Challinor. "It's probably a little bit outside my comfort zone (celebrating).

"It's brilliant to be able to celebrate, but more brilliant to be able to send them home happy. They've been through the mill over the past couple of years, and maybe there's a little bit of a feeling they've got the they've got the football club back.

"You build that camaraderie between the team and supporters by winning and we've done that on the last couple of couple of occasions.

"We need to improve individually, collectively. There's so much more to come.

Sources indicate that "But most importantly for the supporters, they want to see effort. They want to see the team put the bodies on the line. They did that in the second half.".

After too much darkness, they think they can see the light. Barnsley fans are squinting to make it out.

Barnsley: Slicker; Okedina (Reid 86), Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Connell, Kelly (Johnson 86); Brownlie (O'Riordan 90), Yoganathan (Noslin 81), Cleary; Kirk (Toure 81).

Unused substitutes: Ravenhill, Alker.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard (Santos 86), Cooper, Swinkels (Palmer 70); Heskey, Mitchell (Barry 70), Slattery, Bannan (Gray 78), J Lowe (Liongola 70); Keillor-Dunn.

Unused substitutes: Morrison, Trueman.

Referee: O Yates (Staffordshire).

Francesco Camarda could join Cagliari on loan in January and as part of the deal, AC Milan could obtain an option for Paul Mendy, according to a report.

There has been a lot of speculation regarding Camarda’s future in the last few weeks. The 18-year-old has played just 119 minutes so far this season and it’s clear that his development isn’t moving in the right direction as a result.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A loan seems to be the most likely option, especially if Milan were to bring in another striker, but the major question is where he should go. After a so-so loan spell at Lecce, the Rossoneri must evaluate carefully before making their choice.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Cagliari have expressed a concrete interest in securing Camarda on a loan with an option to buy, leaving a buy-back in favour of Milan. In other words, it would be the same formula that was used when he moved to Lecce.

There is one massive difference, though. As per the journalist, the Cagliari striker Paul Mendy could also be involved in the deal. The idea would be to add a ‘buy option’ for Milan, presumably giving them priority to sign the player for a pre-agreed fee.

The 19-year-old has bagged two goals and two assists for the Sardinian side so far, attracting the interest of several clubs (and not just Milan).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in fresh manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

It has been revealed that newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Industry observers note that newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

It has been revealed that the North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Sources indicate that bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

It has been revealed that referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

According to recent reports, A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Sources indicate that elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Sources indicate that chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Industry observers note that newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Industry observers note that newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Sources indicate that rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Sources indicate that newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Recent findings suggest that finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

It has been revealed that lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

In a recent development, that was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

According to recent reports, good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

Sources indicate that on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

In a recent development, leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Sources indicate that newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Recent findings suggest that leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

It has been revealed that fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Newcastle get the game under way.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the latest season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

New manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a massive challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about latest signings.

In a recent development, “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he stated.

Recent findings suggest that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle stated he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

It has been revealed that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he remarked.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

Looking to extend their perfect record in the Champions League campaign,  Real Madrid welcome PSV Eindhoven to the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday night for Matchday Five of the league phase.

Los Blancos, who have won each of their four continental outings this term, have now recorded victories in nine games in a row across all competitions, most recently coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 on Saturday to remain second in the La Liga table.

Bernardo Silva and Aurelien Tchouameni were both available after fitness concerns during the international break, while Vinicius Junior returned from his four-match ban, though Mourinho still has several players unavailable through injury.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Real Madrid's latest injury and suspension news ahead of their meeting with PSV, who travel to the Spanish capital with four points from their opening four Champions League matches.

Rodrygo continues his recovery from an ACL injury and has yet to return to first-team training, with the Brazil international not expected to be back until the start of 2027.

Ferland Mendy had been expected to return against Celta Vigo but was left out of the squad as he continues his recovery from a thigh injury.

The Frenchman is also ineligible to feature against PSV on Tuesday after being omitted from Real Madrid's Champions League squad for the league phase.

Raul Asencio underwent surgery for a stress fracture in his right tibia on October 1 and has made encouraging progress in his recovery, having returned to grass training and ball work.

However, Tuesday's clash with PSV is expected to come too soon for the Spanish defender.

Real Madrid have no suspended players for this match.

Mauricio Pochettino lamented the "completely unfair" decision to send off Leny Yoro in Manchester United's 4-0 thumping at Liverpool on Sunday.

Pochettino made a nightmare start to life as United boss, with a drubbing at the hands of their old rivals, with Yoro's eighth-minute red card setting the tone.

After Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a bouncing ball, Alexander Isak raced in on goal and Yoro clumsily brought him down outside the box, resulting in a straight red card for denying a goal-scoring opportunity.

Dominik Szoboszlai netted from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz turning in an acrobatic volley to double Liverpool's lead three minutes later.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz added gloss to the scoreline in the second half of a dominant display from Liverpool as United struggled to truly test Alisson until first-half stoppage time.

Pochettino insisted Yoro should not have been sent off, believing Isak was not in control at the time of the ball when the challenge happened.

"So, so painful. So disappointed," he told Sky Sports. "It's not in your head to start here in the Premier League in this situation.

"The only problem was that the game changed completely after six minutes, and now we can talk and explain everything, but the damage is done.

Industry observers note that "It's so painful. The players are feeling the pain of this type of situation. I told them they need to be calm, and it was a completely unfair situation that happened.

"And also we need to accept to increase our concentration and also make better decisions on the field, and be much better. We need to be critical of ourselves, but also at the same time, we need to put some situations that happened during the game that we are not happy.

"The ball was going to the keeper. I think in that situation, if you review the VAR, you can see, like we see on the cameras now, that he [Leny Yoro] never had the intention to connect with [Alexander] Isak. The striker saw that the ball was going to the keeper, and he delayed a little bit of his run and goes down.

"But if you go two minutes before. Sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo, they are similar, no? When you compare the actions, that's a penalty, no?

"And if we score after six minutes, for sure we are talking in a different way. But that is sometimes one of the things where we need to take responsibility, and I am here to take responsibility and keep pushing.

"I'm not going to change what happened, and being respectful is always notable. At the same time, I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.".

Mauricio and the team are grateful for your support on a difficult evening at Anfield. A substantial week lies ahead. https://t.co/F6kdP7gz1Z.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 22, 2026.

Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club.

He also suffered the joint-heaviest defeat by a United manager in his first game, along with Lal Halditch, who suffered a 4-0 defeat in October 1926 against Bolton Wanderers in the top-flight.

Accounting for three points per win all-time, United’s eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since 1972-73 (seven), and that tally at the moment leaves them 19th in the table, only one point above bottom-place Crystal Palace.

Pochettino has a mammoth task on his hands to turn things around, but he is determined to get United improving soon.

"I told the players [it was a] completely unfair situation, but when a situation is like this, to turn a negative to positive is we need to make double effort," Pochettino told BBC Sport when asked how his side responded after going 2-0 down so early.

According to recent reports, "More concentration, more focus, care more about everything. We have players, and in a way, after the 12th minute, when we conceded and started to play with 10 men, the players were committed, and they tried everything.

It has been revealed that "We made effort, we ran, we tried. A very difficult team, a team that found the goal when there was the red card. Every day, we will find the possibility to improve.".

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

According to recent reports, at the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri stated Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

According to recent reports, carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Recent findings suggest that kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

Noah Okafor notched a stylish brace as Leeds United dismantled Chelsea - and later paid tribute to the club’s medical staff for getting him fit.

There were plenty of stellar displays as the Whites ran out as 4-1 winners at Stamford Bridge yesterday (November 20).

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Okafor was among Leeds’ star men and scored two of their four goals, first firing across Emiliano Martinez to find the bottom corner and then hammering home from an Ethan Ampadu across.

He now has three goals across his last two games, but it was not long ago the winger was being gnawed at by an injury.

The 26-year-old said: “The last two, three weeks I was struggling a little bit with my adductors and I worked really hard.

Recent findings suggest that “Also a major compliment on the medical staff, like they put me back as quick as possible. I have full trust from the manager, from the whole team, from the whole players. They know my qualities.

“I try to help them with full intensity, with my potential, with my game, how I beat the opponent how I score. Like this, I can help the team. And yeah, when I have the confidence, I can perform. I’m happy about my goals, that I can help the team with this.”.

Okafor is among Leeds’ brightest attacking outlets and has a penchant for rising to the massive occasions. However, he is yet to complete 90 minutes in a Premier League game this season.

He said: “I just have to keep fit, train hard, keep smiling - and then I can help the team every game.”.

Okafor’s late goal gave Leeds a 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur prior to the international break and the Whites picked up where they left off in the capital.

Sources indicate that the wideman’s goals came either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and Brenden Aaronson notched the fourth late on. Prior to the win over Spurs, Leeds had blanked across back-to-back games.

He noted: “It means a lot. I think the hard work in the last days, in the last couple of weeks [paid off]. In some other games, we weren't able to score. That's football.

“We did a lot of draws, so we trained a lot in front of the goal. Today was a back-to-back win and that's why we celebrate.

Recent findings suggest that “We know we have quality up front and also quality behind. We are a strong team. We have a strong mentality. We work hard. And today we gifted ourselves with this [win].”.

‘Get your passports out for Daniel Farke’ was the song of choice as Leeds United dismantled Chelsea in their own backyard, roaring to a 4-1 victory.

Admittedly there was an expletive in that chant to strengthen the sense of enthusiasm, as well as the belief Leeds are ascending to new levels.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that not since December 2002 have Leeds fulfilled a European fixture. Then again, they had not beaten Chelsea at Stamford Bridge since 1999 before they turned up and ran riot. Streaks are there to be ended.

Leeds boss Farke has made a conscious effort to dampen talk of planes and passports, not to spoil the mood but to manage the expectations of an intense fanbase.

By leading his side to a such a convincing victory over a team of expensive global stars, he did not help his campaign of pressure control.

“If you face a side who has world-class potential and world-class potential players, if you dominate the side, then you could label yourself to be more or less from the first to the last second of the game, the better team, it gives lots of belief and lots of confidence,” said Farke. “Yes, of course, it's always good for the mood.

“But it is even more key also for the table to add three more important points, so it's important during this period of the season to collect points in order to make sure that you finish in the right position.

“It will definitely give us more confidence, but to be honest, we also travelled here with confidence and belief, otherwise it wouldn't be possible to show such a dominant performance.”.

Chelsea drew first blood on the 25-minute mark, when the imposing Emmanuel Emegha rifled a shot past James Trafford at the goalkeeper’s near post.

Sources indicate that noah Okafor cancelled out the opener three minutes later - and from there Leeds only grew in confidence. The Swiss winger was to strike again, adding a third after Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s penalty had put the Whites ahead.

By the time Brenden Aaronson weighed in with a fourth from the bench, the party in the away end was well underway.

There is a common narrative when Leeds - or others who threaten the established elites in the Premier League’s upper echelons - gatecrash the top eight.

Pundits and fans have a tendency to focus upon physicality and intensity, sometimes discarding technical and tactical qualities to paint a picture of athletic brutes.

Leeds’ players undoubtedly have robust engines - and they certainly have aggression - but Chelsea were outwitted just as much as they were outfought.

“We looked very, very dominant today in our pressing and with our intensity,” stated Farke. “We always had pressure on the ball, but it has more to do with a tactical blueprint and a tactical solution and how you want to be good against the ball, how you structure your team and also how you want to bypass the opponent than really just fitness level, because on this level all the boys are fit and outstanding.

“If it would be just about physical strength, I would go into the gym and get some bodybuilders and set them on the pitch.”.

There is a widespread acceptance of Farke’s reluctance to discuss Leeds’ potential ceiling - and he is of course right not to get carried away. Leeds are just 11 games in and there will almost certainly be weeks in which they face criticism before the curtain comes down on the 2026/27 campaign.

The music that boomed out of the Leeds dressing room was not quite to Farke’s taste, but he knew better than to pretend it was not fun to bask in the glow of a remarkable afternoon.

It has been revealed that “For me it's a bit too loud,” he remarked. “I'm a bit too old for this.

It has been revealed that “But I'm not dead yet, so sometimes I can also enjoy it a little bit after a game like this. They fully deserve to celebrate themselves. I still remember my time, so after a game like this you would enjoy the night and go out and celebrate and also fully deserve.

“At my age right now, you're looking forward to heading home as soon as possible and I can enjoy a little bit of time on the sofa with coffee and cake.”.

There is not a patisserie in Leeds that would not clear their shelves for Farke after that display.

Chelsea: Martinez, Acheampong (Gusto 73), Fofana, Colwill; Chavarria (Quenda 73); Lavia, Caicedo (Henderson 22); Estevao (Neto 73), Palmer, Rogers; Emegha (Welbeck 64).

Unused substitutes: Penders, Palestra, Suboyole, Barco.

Leeds United: Trafford, Justin, Muharemovic, Elvedi; Bogle (Stach 86), Ampadu, Tanaka (Rodon 86), Gudmundsson; Longstaff (Wilson 90+1), Okafor (Aaronson 73); Calvert-Lewin.

Unused substitutes: Zetterer, Bijol, James, Nmecha.

Referee: Michael Oliver (Northumberland).

#129430. Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 44m • 📚 Deep Dive (8870 w)

Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 44 min read (8870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~44 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4.
  • Unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4.
  • It has been revealed that the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7,8,9,10,11,12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

Unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4. Depending on the relative weight of those energy terms, many different phenomena have been observed: the Hofstadter butterfly depending mainly on the van der Waals coupling13,14,15, commensurate–incommensurate phase transitions driven by van der Waals–strain competition5,6 and flat-band formation that probably involves all three contributions and facilitates superconductivity and correlated insulating phase 16,17,18.

It has been revealed that the particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies. Varying their relative contributions can switch the system between different atomic arrangements, resulting in structural phase transitions potentially accompanied by the emergence of newly introduced electronic phases. This points to a rich underlying phase diagram. Yet experimental platforms that allow controlled exploration of this phase space so far have been lacking.

Here we demonstrate that, by careful tuning of the balance between these competing interactions in a three-layer van der Waals heterostructure, we can reach simultaneous structural and electronic phase transitions, controlled through layer charging, magnetic field or temperature variation. We engineer these transitions in a heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hBN and mhBN on either side: mhBN/graphene/hBN. In such heterostructures, strain is greatly enhanced because mhBN, unlike its bulk counterpart, is free to contract and corrugate (the strain amplitude is controlled by the number of hBN layers), leading to strongly enhanced surface reconstruction19,20,21. The van der Waals interaction of this system is likewise enhanced by the double alignment and can be tuned by gate-charging the graphene layer.

It has been revealed that in such heterostructure devices, the structural phase transition reveals itself through an abrupt, global and reversible switch of the stacking configuration, which entails a change of symmetry (analogous to the Bernal-to-rhombohedral transition in graphite22,23,24,25) and results in distinct reconstruction modes observed directly by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). It is accompanied by a unique electronic phase transition: switching between p-doping and n-doping of graphene. Unlike conventional doping, the doping levels before and after the phase transition are discrete rather than continuous in nature, always taking an integer or ‘quantized’ value corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons per moiré unit cell, which we hereafter term integer doping. We attribute this integer doping to electrons (holes) being trapped in the strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (PLLs), formed by the strong moiré surface reconstruction; these localized states constitute flat bands in k-space, as predicted theoretically7,8,9,10,11 and confirmed by STM measurements12. The structural transition alters the atomic arrangement, modifying both the strain and scalar-potential landscapes. In reciprocal space, we interpret this as switching the hybridization of these flat bands between the valence band (AB phase) and the conduction band (AA phase), inverting the sign of the integer doping.

Our heterostructure consists of monolayer graphene that is double-aligned, on one side to hBN and on the other side to mhBN (refs. 19,20). Unlike single alignment, such double-aligned ‘sandwich’ heterostructures can exhibit either parallel or antiparallel orientations corresponding to the 0° and 180° angle alignment between the top and bottom hBN (refs. 2,19,26). The results obtained on both types of device are similar, so in the main text, we focus on the parallel orientation, presenting the analysis for the antiparallel orientation in Supplementary Information Sections 20, 23, 26 and 28 (Supplementary Figs. 30, 41 and 42).

For either orientation, two energetically competing stacking configurations exist (Fig. 1c,d), which are interconvertible by sliding the mhBN by one interatomic distance relative to the bulk hBN (detailed explanation and simple schematics in Supplementary Information Section 21; Supplementary Figs. 31 and 32). This is analogous to the transition between ABC (rhombohedral) and ABA (Bernal) trilayer graphene, in which a small shift of one of the layers leads to strong reconfigurations of the electronic bands22,23,24,25.

According to recent reports, a, Schematic representation of the full phase diagram formed in our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN system. External parameters (such as carrier density n, magnetic field B and temperature T) define one coordinate axis, whereas the intrinsic stacking order of the sandwich heterostructure defines the other. Two local energy minima exist corresponding to AA and AB stacking configurations, with their dominant stackings shown in c and d, respectively. Blue and red arrows indicate transitions between these configurations; solid arrows denote states realized under continuous tuning of external parameters, whereas dashed arrows mark the abrupt structural phase transition, matching the solid and dashed lines in the experiments shown in Fig. 3a–c. b, Moiré-induced corrugation observed in a double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN device, measured at room temperature by AFM. Inset shows the corrugation profile along the light blue line. Phonon squeezing reduces corrugation at low temperatures. The unit cell outlined in black matches that in g. c,d, Schematic illustrations of the competing sandwich configurations at double-aligned interfaces: AB (c) and AA (d) stacking configurations. e–h, MD simulations of strain distributions. Panels g and h show our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN configurations with AB and AA stacking configurations, respectively, and panels e and f show reference calculations for double-aligned hBN/graphene/hBN configurations. Comparison highlights the notable role of mhBN on strain enhancement, leading to much stronger reconstruction patterns—triangular and hexagonal reconstructions, respectively. Dashed circles indicate vertices of domains arising from these two reconstruction types, on which strain-induced PLLs develop, as shown on the right. The yellow-to-orange gradient bar indicates increasing strain amplitude. i, The theoretical calculated corrugation of the graphene–hBN interface as a function of the twist angle.

It has been revealed that unlike previous studies that apply a mechanical tool such as an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope tip to locally ‘iron’ the sample to toggle the stacking configurations in confined regions of sample27,28, our system allows global, reversible switching between the two stacking states simply by tuning external parameters, including carrier density n, magnetic field B or temperature T. Such all-electronic control is far better suited to device integration and to triggering newly introduced phenomena in transport measurements. The schematic in Fig. 1a illustrates the full phase diagram defined by these external parameters and the intrinsic stacking order, in which the two local minima correspond to the competing AB and AA stacking configurations. Accompanying this switch, the moiré-induced strain distribution and thus the lattice reconstruction changes from triangular to hexagonal patterns (Fig. 1e–h; see also the STM images in Fig. 5a,b), ultimately leading to different pseudomagnetic field (PMF) distributions2,29 (Fig. 5e,f) and different band reconfigurations (Fig. 5g–j).

In a recent development, we emphasize that the mhBN is essential for enhancing such lattice reconstruction of graphene, as mhBN itself can accommodate a finite amount of strain, allowing both layers (mhBN and graphene) to undergo very strong relaxation. The molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, comparing mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1g,h) and hBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1e,f) heterostructures, clearly demonstrate that the presence of mhBN greatly amplifies the periodic strain induced by moiré reconstruction. The experimental evidence, including room-temperature atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurement of the corrugation (Fig. 1b) and the same measurement with varying hBN layer numbers (1–4 layers; Supplementary Information Section 13; Supplementary Fig. 19) and their corresponding transport properties, is presented in Supplementary Information Section 4. As well as mhBN, alignment also markedly influences the strain, as shown by the calculated corrugation with respect to the twist angle in Fig. 1i.

According to recent reports, two types of transport device are discussed in the main text: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN (Fig. 2a) and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 2b). In the former, the mhBN–hBN interface is intentionally misaligned by 15° to achieve superlubricity, preserving the double-aligned sandwich structure. The two architectures are complementary: the dual-gated capped devices enable higher carrier concentrations and allow the roles of doping and the displacement field to be disentangled (Supplementary Information Section 8), whereas the non-capped mhBN/graphene/hBN structure develops stronger reconstruction, in particular the out-of-plane corrugation at the graphene–mhBN interface (Supplementary Information Section 30).

a, Schematic of the transport device with hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN heterostructure (inset) in a dual-graphite gate configuration. b, Schematic of the mhBN/graphene/hBN transport device. The unencapsulated mhBN enables AFM measurement. Inset, AFM image of the device (bottom right) and its fast Fourier transform (FFT). The FFT confirms the double alignment and gives the periods of both superlattices, which agree well with those derived from the transport measurement in d. Scale bar, 50 nm. c,d, Longitudinal resistance Rxx of the states before (blue) and after (red) the transition in the device types in a and b, measured at T = 1.6 K. The neutrality point, labelled ‘NP’, shifts from no doping to n-doping (device in a) and from p-doping to n-doping (device in b) on transition. The top axis marks doping levels corresponding to integer multiples of electrons or holes per moiré unit cell. The doping shift relative to zero is denoted by Δnint, in which ‘int’ signifies intrinsic doping (in contrast to external doping by gate). For the device in a, the bottom axis (Vdual D = 0) is defined such that both Vtg and Vbg are simultaneously tuned to vary carrier density while maintaining zero displacement field in graphene. By contrast, the device in b has only back gate, so its bottom axis is represented by Vbg. e,f, The doping levels of other same-structured devices with different periods of moiré plaquette λm before (blue dots) and after (red dots) transition. The details of all samples are presented in Supplementary Information Section 3 and Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6. The doping levels of all samples, before and after the transition, are located at integer multiples of electrons per moiré unit cell, with the percentage deviation from ideal integer multiples (Δnint − Nn0)/Nn0 shown by bar graphs at the corresponding positions, in which Δnint − Nn0 is the deviation from the nearest integer multiple N (if N is 0, then we choose the denominator Nn0 = n0).

Recent findings suggest that for both architectures, double alignment of graphene to the hBN crystals on both sides was confirmed by AFM, Raman and transport measurements (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 2). We emphasize that both the double alignment and the presence of mhBN are crucial for the effects we observe, as corroborated by seven types of reference device, none of which exhibit the transition (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4; Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

Industry observers note that first, let us examine the initial-state transfer curves (blue) of the two device types in Fig. 2c,d. In the hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN sample, the neutrality point of graphene remains at zero doping, whereas the mhBN/graphene/hBN structure exhibits p-doping. Notably, this p-doping level closely approximates 2n0 (n0 corresponds to doping of one charge carrier per moiré plaquette). In 8 of 9 unencapsulated mhBN/graphene/hBN devices (blue dots in Fig. 2f), the p-doping is quantized at Nn0 (N is an integer between 1 and 4), growing with the moiré period but always fixed at integer multiples of n0.

Sources indicate that in Fig. 2e,f, the moiré period, determined from the carrier density of secondary Dirac points, exceeds in many samples the rigid-lattice limit of 14 nm (set by the 1.8% graphene–hBN lattice mismatch) and even reaches 17.7 nm, a consequence of the strain enhancement by mhBN and double alignment19,20 (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4).

In a recent development, by applying a large positive gate voltage above a certain threshold, a phase transition can be initiated: the moiré period remains unchanged but the samples become n-doped, again by an integer number of electrons per moiré plaquette, for both bottom-gated and dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c,d), and consistently across samples with different moiré sizes (Fig. 2e,f; Supplementary Information Section 3; Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). Comprehensive control experiments (Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14; Supplementary Figs. 9–11 and 20–22) verify that this transition and the integer doping are intrinsic, excluding artefacts such as contamination. We emphasize that the integer doping is a direct observation requiring no fitting or registration procedure. As is well established for graphene superlattices5,6,7, the neutrality point–secondary Dirac point separation is fixed at four electrons per moiré unit cell. In Fig. 2c, the post-transition neutrality point (red) falls precisely at the midpoint between the pre-transition neutrality point and the secondary Dirac point (blue) and hence corresponds to exactly two electrons per moiré unit cell, as highlighted by the equally spaced ruler.

Note that for the dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c), the gate voltage was applied simultaneously through top and bottom gates along the D = 0 line30 (dashed line in Fig. 3a). The switching depends only on the total carrier concentration and not on the displacement field (Supplementary Information Section 8; Supplementary Fig. 14). This mechanism fundamentally differs from recently reported two-dimensional ferroelectric systems, in which transitions occur through external electric-field-induced polarization changes26,31,32.

a–c, Vtg–Vbg maps of the transition process, each obtained by sweeping Vbg at stepped Vtg; a–c differ in gate sweep range and sweep history (marked by orange arrows). Orange arrows: sweep directions of top gate (Vtg) and back gate (Vbg). Blue and red arrows or solid lines represent Dirac points before and after transition, respectively. Numbers for blue lines and arrows give the doping per moiré unit cell at neutrality point (NP, 0), secondary Dirac points (SDP, ±4), tertiary Dirac points (TDP, ±8) and quaternary Dirac points (QDP, ±12); numbers for red lines and arrows are the same points offset by −2 electrons. Dashed lines indicate abrupt state changes at transition. The dashed black line in a denotes zero displacement field (D = 0), along which all transfer curves in Figs. 2 and 3 were performed; all forward and reverse transitions in a–c occur on this line, indicating that the displacement field is not the driving mechanism. In a–c, the transition point and the post-transition state are independent of gate range and sweep history. d, Continuous monitoring of the transition. Blue (5.3 V) and red (−6.9 V) dashed lines mark the critical voltages for transition and reversal, respectively. Black arrows track the measurement sequence (swp1–swp8); blue and red denote sweepings starting from the ‘before transition’ and ‘after transition’ states, respectively. Central dashed lines correspond to Δnint/n0 = 0, −4 (blue) and −2 and −6 (red). Shaded region above swp8 represents more than 100 repeated forward/reverse gate sweeps, after which the sample remains unchanged. e, Vdual D = 0–B maps, obtained through Vdual sweeps at fixed magnetic field steps. Orange arrows: sweep and field-variation directions (13 T to 0 T). The Vdual D = 0 sweep range surpasses the critical voltage of the forward transition (dashed blue line at 5.3 V) but not the reverse (dashed red line at −6.9 V) in d. Blue and red solid lines are states before and after transition, respectively. Notably, transition occurs at 3.8 T, at which magnetic length (approximately 13.4 nm) becomes commensurate with moiré periodicity. f,g, Zoom-in views of the blue and red boxed regions in d, respectively, revealing abrupt state changes at critical voltages (dashed lines). Circles represent the plotted resistance points; arrows indicate transition-induced resistance jump. h, Correlation between Rxx and Rxy; top axis, measured Hall density nfree; bottom axis, total gate-induced charge ntotal. The Hall zero-crossing (nfree = 0) occurs at ntotal = 2 holes per moiré cell, the difference being the localized charge nloc.

It has been revealed that to investigate the transition dynamics and reproducibility, we conducted a series of Vtg–Vbg mappings and repeated switching tests (Rxx in Fig. 3; Rxy in Supplementary Fig. 24). Figure 3a–c reveals several Dirac points separated by intervals of four electrons per moiré plaquette5,6,7, marked with blue (before transition) or red (after transition) lines or arrows.

It has been revealed that the phase transition occurs at Vtg = +3.9 V, Vbg = +5.3 V corresponding to ntotal = 3.75 × 1012 cm−2 along the D = 0 line in Fig. 3a. Following the transition, all features shift by two electrons per moiré plaquette. This shift throughout the entire superlattice spectrum clearly indicates that the moiré period is unchanged. The recovery occurs at Vtg = −5.0 V, Vbg = −6.9 V (corresponding to −4.85 × 1012 cm−2), also along the D = 0 line, restoring the entire gate dependence (Fig. 3b). Comparing Fig. 3c with Fig. 3a shows that different Vtg–Vbg ranges and sweep protocols do not affect the transition characteristics: it occurs at identical gate points, as a single discrete event at the critical voltage rather than a continuous evolution.

Figure 3d illustrates the transition dynamics through sequential measurements (swp1–swp8), with dashed lines at +5.3 V and −6.9 V marking the critical voltages for the forward and reverse transitions, respectively. Below the critical voltage, no transition occurs (swp1–swp2); on reaching it, the transition happens (swp3–swp4), at a critical voltage independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15; Supplementary Fig. 23). Similar behaviour is observed for the reverse transition (steps swp4–swp7). Figure 3f,g demonstrates zoomed-in views around the critical voltages for both the forward and reverse transitions. At the moment of transition, the resistance jumps from one state to another without any intermediate states, consistent with the abrupt translation of features observed in Vtg–Vbg mappings of Fig. 3a–c. Once the transition is induced, further increasing the gate voltage yields no continuous effect, indicating a saturation mechanism defined by the moiré unit cell capacity rather than the strength of the applied field. This behaviour differs markedly from that of ferroelectrics, for which polarization scales continuously with the applied field. The switching is fully reproducible: 100 consecutive cycles yield curves that overlap precisely (Fig. 3d, top). All behaviours discussed above support that the observed phase transition is a first-order-like transition (further information in Supplementary Information Section 43).

Recent findings suggest that notably, the transition can also be controlled by the magnetic field. Mapping the transition from 13 T down to 0 T (Fig. 3e) highlights that the transition is suppressed at high field, even for gate voltages far exceeding the critical value, and reappears at exactly the same critical voltage once the field drops below Bcrit = 3.8 T. The origin of this suppression remains to be established; we note, however, that the magnetic length at critical field \(\sqrt{\hbar /e{B}_{{\rm{crit}}}}\approx 13.4\,{\rm{nm}}\) is comparable with the moiré period for this sample of 13.8 nm.

Recent findings suggest that in Fig. 3h, correlating Rxx with Rxy gives further information for theoretical analysis: the Hall-resistivity zero crossing (zero free carrier density nfree) occurs at a gate-induced density of two holes per moiré unit cell, the difference being compensated by localized electrons nloc.

To identify the origin of the phase transition, we consider the balance between elastic (strain) and van der Waals forces5,6, which can be modified through Coulomb interactions introduced by gate charging the graphene layer.

Industry observers note that using high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), we calculated the adhesion-energy distribution across the non-relaxed moiré plaquette, assuming perfect alignment of hBN on both sides, for the AB (Fig. 4a) and AA (Fig. 4b) relative configurations of the two hBN crystals (Supplementary Information Section 22; Supplementary Figs. 33–35). The relative energy of the two configurations can be compared by averaging the van der Waals potential over the entire moiré unit cell, as illustrated in Fig. 4c. The AB structure exhibits lower energy under neutral charging conditions (Fig. 4c–e). However, by assigning a negative charge on graphene above a certain threshold (corresponding to positive gate voltage applied) the AA configuration becomes more energetically favourable than AB (Fig. 4c,f,g), resulting in a structural phase transition from AB to AA.

Sources indicate that a,b, Schematics of the two configurations (AB (a) and AA (b)) and three high-symmetry stacking sites for both configurations. The red arrows on the left side indicate a shift of one of the hBN layers by one interatomic distance. c, Schematic diagram of the relative stability (in terms of the average adhesion energy taken over the entire moiré plaquette) of the two configurations as a function of doping. The solid lines represent the energy-favourable state. The crossing of the blue and red lines indicates the occurrence of the transition. Electron doping (positive gate) switches the relative stability between the two configurations and the consequent modification of the interlayer adhesion is proposed to be the driving force. d–g, Distribution of the interlayer adhesion energy (Eadh) across the moiré plaquette for the AB (d,f) and AA (e,g) configurations in the case of zero (d,e) and n-type (f,g) external doping (induced by gating in our experiments). The graphs in the middle give the corresponding adhesion energies of the three high-symmetry stackings as a function of interlayer distance between graphene and the top and bottom boron nitride layers near the equilibrium spacing (2.7–4.0 Å).

The energy evolution with doping arises from gate-introduced Coulomb interactions, which enter the competition between van der Waals forces and elastic energies5,6. The balance among these three factors can be understood by comparing the relative stability of the AB and AA stacking configurations at high-symmetry points (Fig. 4a,b), which are the most representative sites and capture the qualitative trends under gating. Specifically, n-type doping substantially reduces the interlayer potential of AA-3 stacking: there, carbon atoms are vertically aligned with boron and the added electrons on carbon are strongly attracted to the positive charge on boron arising from the ionic nature of B–N bonds33. By contrast, the interlayer potential of AA-2 stacking is slightly elevated by the repulsion between the added electrons and the negatively charged nitrogen, whereas AA-1 and all three high-symmetry sites of the AB alignment remain almost unchanged, as the interaction of added electrons with boron is compensated by their interaction with nitrogen. This picture is substantiated by DFT calculations (Fig. 4d–g; Supplementary Information Sections 22–27). We can generalize the similar gate-induced phase transitions to other systems in which at least one of the multiply aligned layers has electropolarity (Supplementary Information Section 37).

We now turn to the origin of the integer doping in graphene, which we attribute to strain-induced PLLs localized at the vertices of the reconstructed moiré domains. The reconstructed phases for AB and AA configurations are directly visualized through STM measurements (STM images of different regions, and of a reference single-aligned graphene/hBN region on the same flake, are shown in Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13) and theoretically simulated by MD calculations (Fig. 5a,b). On the basis of the atomic displacements calculated by MD, we obtained the strain distribution in the reconstructed moiré unit cell (schematics shown in Fig. 5c,d), as well as the associated pseudomagnetic field7,8,9,10,11,34 (left panels of Fig. 5e,f) (Supplementary Information Sections 24, 29 and 31).

Industry observers note that the reconstruction results in distinct strain fields for the AB and AA configurations (Fig. 5c,d). For the AB configuration, it is the AB-1 and AB-3 stackings that have much lower energy than AB-2 (Fig. 4d,f), so the reconstruction forms triangular domains of AB-1 and AB-3 stackings, accompanied by notable strain and out-of-plane corrugation at the AB-2 stacking (Fig. 5c). By contrast, for the AA configuration, it is the AA-3 stacking that has the lowest energy (Fig. 4e,g), leading to hexagonally reconstructed AA-3 moiré domain, with the strain concentrated at AA-2 and AA-1 stacked corners of the moiré plaquette (Fig. 5d). Here the predominance of in-plane strain in AA (versus out-of-plane corrugation in AB) originates from the mirror symmetry of the AA configuration, which yields negligible net out-of-plane force (Supplementary Information Section 38; Supplementary Fig. 54). In both cases, the strain results in strong PMF.
