In a recent development, for starburst amacrine cell (Chat+) ablation experiments, AAV2-Flex-taCasp3-TEVp was injected into the left eye or both eyes of mice in the ablation groups. 2 sites located at the dorsal and ventral parts of the eyeball were used for injection; 0.75 µl of virus was injected into each site. For the control groups, same volume of saline was injected into the left eye of mice. Two-photon calcium imaging was performed 1 month after injection.

For adult SC labelling, mice were anaesthetized with isoflurane during the surgery (3% for induction and 1.5–2% for maintenance) and placed in a stereotaxic apparatus (Model 940, David Kopf Instruments). Meloxicam (5 mg kg−1) was administered intraperitoneally for analgesia before the surgery and 1 day after the surgery. Body temperature was maintained at 37 °C using a homeothermic blanket. Viral solutions were loaded into a pulled glass pipette connected to a syringe (7634-0, Hamilton) via a dual-ferrule adaptor (55750-0, Hamilton). The injection speed and volume were controlled by a Microinjection Syringe Pump (UMP3T-1, WPI). AAV2-EF1a-FDIO-mCherry or AAV2-EF1a-FDIO-EGFP (1 µl) was injected into the right SC of adult mice at a constant speed (60 nl min−1).

Two injection sites were used for the Cdh7-FlpO and Cbln4-FlpO lines: one at 0.35 mm posterior and 0.5 mm lateral to lambda at a depth of 1.3 mm, and the other at 0.1 mm posterior and 0.6 mm lateral to lambda at a depth of 1.2 mm. The mice were transcardially perfused at 4 wpi. The brains were collected for immunohistochemical analysis. In addition, specifically for pseudorabies-mediated retrograde tracing, AAV8-hSyn-FRT-TVA-P2A-EGFP-2A-oG viruses (1 µl) were injected into the right SC of the Cdh7-FlpO or Cbln4-FlpO adult mice by stereotaxic injections as described above. Three weeks later, EnvA G-Deleted Rabies-mCherry (1.2 µl) was injected into the right SC. Six days post-rabies injection, mice were transcardially perfused, and brains and contralateral (left) retinas were collected for immunohistochemical analysis.

We used the Cre/FlpO strategy to label SC neurons and manipulate RGCs separately by crossing RGC-specific Cre drivers to SC-specific FlpO mice. After injecting AAV2-EF1α-FDIO-GFP-WPRE into the right SC of Cbln4-FlpO or Cdh7-FlpO mice, we can target recording from GFP-labelled SC neurons. By injecting AAV2-CAG-ChR2-mCherry-WPRE to manipulate all RGCs or AAV2-EF1α-DIO-ChR2(H134R)-mCherry to manipulate specific types of RGCs into the left eye, a blue light (473 nm, 15 mW mm−2) can activate the RGC axon terminals in the SC.

Industry observers note that injected mice were anaesthetized by ketamine and xylazine (100 mg kg−1, 12.5 mg kg−1) and transcardially perfused with ice-cold Cutting solution (78.3 mM NaCl, 2.3 mM KCl, 33.8 mM choline-Cl, 0.45 mM CaCl2, 6.4 mM MgCl2, 1.1 mM NaH2PO4, 23 mM NaHCO3, 20 mM D-glucose, 0.5 mM L-glutamine, pH 7.4). The brains were dissected, and coronal brain sections were prepared using a vibratome (VT1200S, Leica) in ice-cold, carbogenated Cutting solution. Slices (250 μm in thickness) with SC were collected and transferred to a 32.5 °C incubation chamber filled with carbogenated Cutting solution. After 30 min incubation, the slices were transferred to room temperature artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF; 125 mM NaCl, 2.5 mM KCl, 1.25 mM NaH2PO4, 26 mM NaHCO3, 1 mM MgCl2·6H2O, 2 mM CaCl2, 20 mM D-glucose, pH 7.4) before recording. Cutting solutions and ACSF were constantly bubbled with 5% CO2 and 95% O2 (Carbogen, Airgas).

A CCD camera (IR-2000, DAGE-MTI) mounted on a fluorescence microscope (BX51WI, Olympus) was used to detect a green cell surrounded by red axon terminals. Targeted whole-cell recordings were made under IR-DIC visualization. The glass pipettes (BF150-86-10, Sutter Instrument) were pulled by a puller (P1000, Sutter Instrument) into recording electrodes (3–5 MΩ). The recording electrode was filled with potassium-based internal solutions (135 mM potassium gluconate, 8 mM KCl, 10 mM HEPES, 0.25 mM EGTA, 2 mM MgATP, 0.3 mM Na2GTP, 7 mM phosphocreatine, pH 7.3). All data were acquired using a MultiClamp 700B Amplifier and a 1440A DigiData (Molecular Devices). The signals were digitized at 10 kHz and low-pass filtered at 1 kHz. Axon activation was performed using a 473 nm LED (Cool LED, pE300). Five light pulses (2 ms) were delivered per trial. After breaking into the cells, we held them at −65 mV and applied whole-cell compensation. Voltage-clamp mode was used to record evoked EPSCs, and current-clamp mode was used to record action potentials. Tetrodotoxin (TTX, 1 µM) and 4-aminopyridine (4-AP, 100 µM) were added to ACSF perfusions to confirm the monosynaptic connection. CNQX (10 µM) and APV (50 µM) were added to confirm the glutamatergic synapses. For experiments in which multiple neurons were recorded from the same mouse, mouse identity was treated as the experimental unit or random effect to account for the hierarchical structure of the data.

It has been revealed that an internal solution containing Biocytin (0.5%, B4261-100mg, Sigma) was used for electrophysiological recording and dye filling, as previously described71. After recording, brain slices were fixed with 4% PFA overnight at 4 °C, then blocked with blocking solution (PBS with 0.3% TritonX-100 and 5% normal donkey serum) for one day at 4 °C. Then the slices were incubated with Streptavidin-488 or 555 (1:1,000, Invitrogen) for 2 h at room temperature. After mounting the slices, the images were acquired by a Zeiss confocal microscope (LSM900).

In vivo calcium imaging of mouse SC was performed using a two-photon microscope as previously described72.

Recent findings suggest that surgeries were performed on eight-week-old transgenic mice. The craniotomy, virus injection, and transparent silicone plug insertion were done over the right SC. Mice were anaesthetized with ketamine and xylazine and placed in a stereotaxic device with their eyes covered with ophthalmic ointment. Mice were anaesthetized with 2% isoflurane for maintenance and injected with meloxicam (5 mg kg−1). Craniotomy was performed over the lambda of the skull, and a large flap was opened in the dura with a forceps (Dumoxel-Biology 11252-30, FST). We injected the right SC with 400 nl of AAV8-EF1α-FDIO-GCaMP6s. A silicone plug bonded to a 5 mm circular coverslip was mounted on a suction cup and positioned over the craniotomy. The plug advanced downward to press the brain and then anteriorly to displace the dura and transverse sinuses. A drop of cyanoacrylate (Vetbond, 3 M) was used to fix the silicon plug to the skull, then the suction was released, and the suction cup was withdrawn. A custom head plate (titanium, 1 mm thick, eMachineShop) was bonded to the skull by cyanoacrylate (Vetbond, 3 M) and dental cement (Ortho-Jet, LangDental). At least 2 weeks after implanting cranial windows, mice were habituated to handling and head-fixing at least 4 times under a two-photon microscope.

Sources indicate that we imaged calcium responses in mice using a two-photon microscope (Neurolabware) with a Spectra-Physics MaiTai laser at 920 nm (15–50 mW) to excite GCaMP6s. Imaging in the SC was performed at depths of 50–200 µm below the pia surface. A 575 × 370 µm field of view was scanned at 15.5 Hz, producing a series of 416 × 268-pixel images. A tangent LCD screen (Dell, U2312HM) placed in front of the left eye of head-fixed mice will present a visual stimulus generated with Psychtoolbox3 (MATLAB) and synchronized with image acquisition via TTL signals from the stimulus screen. The screen is centred 14 cm away from the mouse, angled at 20 degrees in pitch and yaw to minimize fisheye distortion. We imaged each mouse for about 1 h, with multiple sessions on successive days if needed to present a battery of visual stimuli and acquire stable imaging.

Industry observers note that visual stimuli were presented on a tangent (1,920 × 1,080 pixels) region of the screen. The screen was strobed for 2 µs at the end of each scan line (1,200 Hz; luminance of the grey screen, 1.25 cd m−2; maximum brightness, 1/80 of the unmodified monitor) to minimize interference between the visual stimulus and two-photon fluorescence detection. All stimuli presented used only the green and blue channels of the screen. Red bars flickered periodically at the bottom of the screen, which was covered with black tape, to convey the timing of the visual stimulus to synchronize with fluorescence acquisition. All visual stimuli in two-photon experiments were presented in a pseudorandom sequence, interspersed with blank periods within each stimulus block, using a different random seed for each block. Moving gratings were used to test the direction selectivity of SC neurons. The drifting grating was 100 pixels wide (6.4°), with black or white bars, and drifted in 8 directions (45° intervals) at a speed of 356 pixels per second (22.7° per second). To map receptive fields, flashing spots were presented in a 9 × 5 position arrayed across the stimulus monitor. Each spot was a 216 × 216 pixel (13.8° × 13.8°) square that appeared for 1 second. All visual stimuli were repeated six times per trial.

To test the contribution of the ipsilateral eye to the direction selectivity of Cbln4+ SC neurons, we covered the ipsilateral eye with a black box during calcium imaging. The box was removed after the experiments.

We performed offline motion correction of calcium imaging data by NoRMCorre73, identified GCaMP6s+ cells, extracted calcium traces for each cell, and subtracted neuropil signals. Next, we aligned traces to visual stimuli using synchronization pulses relayed from stimulus monitors to the microscope via a TTL signal, which were time-stamped in the imaging data. For traces with high-peak noisy spikes (large mouse motion that cannot be corrected), we used a denoising algorithm to replace noisy dots with smooth traces. The noisy spike traces were determined by whether any points were bigger than the mean ± 4 s.d. traces. Then, calcium traces were aligned to the onset of each visual stimulus, averaged across trials, and the peak and valley of each mean trace were identified.

DSI calculation followed a previously published protocol74. ΔF/F values for each presentation of a stimulus were averaged from six repeats, and the peak ΔF/F for each direction was used to compute direction preference. The direction selectivity index (DSI) was calculated as the normalized amplitude of the vector sum of all directions by their scalar sum. Cells with DSI > 0.2 were classified as direction selective. The preferred direction was defined as the weighted vector sum over eight stimulus angles.

According to recent reports, for confocal image acquisition, all procedures were conducted in a double-blind manner. One researcher collected images without knowledge of genotype, while a second researcher, who performed the analysis, was also blinded. Littermates were used as controls in all experiments unless otherwise indicated. Both male and female mice were included. Images were acquired on a Zeiss LSM900 confocal microscope (Carl Zeiss Microscopy) equipped with 10× air, 20× air and 40× oil immersion objectives.

To quantify immunostained cells in the SC and retina, confocal images of vertical retinal sections, coronal SC sections, and whole-mount retina were collected under identical imaging conditions across all samples. Confocal stacks of 20 µm (retina and SC sections) or 60 µm (whole-mount retina) were acquired and processed to generate maximum-intensity projections. Cells positive for each marker was identified using thresholded fluorescence intensity criteria. Single-positive and double-positive cells were manually counted with the Cell Counter plugin in ImageJ (NIH). For RNAscope in situ hybridization, SC sections processed with RNAscope and immunostaining were imaged on a Zeiss LSM900 with a 20× objective. The number of GFP-positive neurons or marker-positive cells was counted across all stained samples as mentioned above. Data were pooled across animals, and results are presented as percentages (mean ± s.e.m.). Confocal image files for histology were analysed using Fiji Image J (v1.53c), Microsoft Excel 365, Graph Pad Prism9, Adobe Illustrator 2020. Electrophysiological data collection and analysis were not performed blindly with respect to the experimental conditions. All whole-cell recording data were acquired by Camplex 10.7 (Molecular Devices) and analysed in MATLAB (MathWorks) or Clampfit 10.7 (Molecular Devices). Optogenetically evoked currents were averaged across 5 trials. Clampfit 10.7 measured the peak amplitudes of evoked currents. MATLAB analysed the intrinsic properties of recorded neurons. All statistics were calculated by GraphPad Prism 9. Peak currents between the two groups were compared using a two-tailed Student’s t-test.

It has been revealed that optomotor response was described previously75. The OptoDrum (Striatech) comprises a box with four screens to simulate drifting gratings. An IR camera mounted on the top of the box was used to record mouse movements. Mice were first acclimated to the room in their cages for 30 min. Then, freely moving mice were placed on a platform and allowed to acclimate to the box for at least 5 min. Drifting gratings (12° s−1) in the clockwise direction can trigger left-eye-mediated body and head movements, while drifting gratings in the counterclockwise direction were used to test right-eye-mediated movements. Drifting gratings were presented from low spatial frequencies (0.056 cycles per degree) to high frequencies (0.3–0.5 cycles per degree) to determine the threshold at which a mouse could track. OptoDrum’s software can detect the body shape of mice and label the positions of head, body, and tail of mice. The stimulus and video tracking were paused if a mouse engaged in grooming behaviour or dropped off the platform and resumed later. The software can score the optomotor response and determine the spatial-frequency threshold. False positives were manually identified as invalid, and the same frequency of drifting gratings was repeated. We compared the spatial-frequency threshold of drifting gratings to trigger optomotor responses in the left eye (ablation) with the right eye (control) to assess visual acuity differences.

We obtained measurements from distinct biological samples. No covariates were tested. No formal test of normality was performed; statistical tests were selected based on the distributional assumptions of the data. Statistical methods and the number of animals tested for each configuration are documented in the figure legends for each experiment. When comparing two groups, statistics were derived using an unpaired two-sided Student’s t-test, Kolmogorov–Smirnov test or Fisher’s exact test, as indicated in the figure legends. For comparing cell-type proportions across multiple reactions, we used the Kruskal–Wallis H test (scipy.stats.kruskal, Python). One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed in GraphPad Prism 9 to assess the statistical significance of differences among multiple measurements.

Fisher’s exact test was performed using the Easy Fisher Exact Test Calculator (https://www.socscistatistics.com/tests/fisher/default2.aspx).

Sources indicate that statistical significance was defined as *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001 and ****P < 0.0001. All values indicate mean ± s.e.m., unless otherwise noted.

a, Unsupervised classification of sSC using the standard fresh-frozen MERFISH protocol. UMAP embedding of 5,845 cells reveals consistent clustering of the same 8 ENCs and 11 INCs identified with TransA-MERFISH on fixed tissue (Fig. 1d). Cell-type labels were assigned to Leiden clusters based on canonical marker gene expression patterns and transcriptomic mapping via a supervised XGBoost classifier trained on the TransA-MERFISH atlas. b, Confusion matrix showing transcriptomic correspondence between cell types in standard MERFISH (rows) and TransA-MERFISH (columns). c, Violin plots comparing quality control metrics between standard MERFISH (blue) and TransA-MERFISH (gray). Distributions are highly similar across key metrics, including the number of genes detected per cell (n_genes_by_counts), total transcript counts per cell (total_counts), and cell mask area (in pixels). A modest reduction in n_genes_by_counts and total_counts was observed in TransA-MERFISH experiments. d, Comparison of matched neuronal subtype frequencies between standard MERFISH and TransA-MERFISH. Values are plotted on a ln-ln scale to highlight low-frequency types. A strong correlation is observed across both excitatory and inhibitory populations, indicating that the TransA-MERFISH protocol did not bias or deplete neuron types in the sSC (Pearson R = 0.88). e, Validation accuracies of the XGBoost classifier trained using various gene selection strategies: the performance of the 140-gene TransA-MERFISH panel was compared to randomly sampled 140-gene sets drawn from either the full single-cell transcriptome or the top 2000 highly variable genes (HVGs). Additional gene sets were constructed by selecting the top k specific genes (Methods) per SC neuronal cluster (k = 1–10), based on 19 neuronal clusters identified from re-clustering of the neuronal subset of the dataset28. Data are presented as mean ± SD. f, Dot plots comparing the expression patterns of 2 non-optimal probes (top row, blue) with their corresponding expressions in snRNA-seq17 (bottom row, orange). MERFISH cells are grouped according to their predicted snRNA-seq cluster identities, as inferred by Tangram-based imputation (Methods). The 140-gene list is presented in Supplementary Table 1. g-j, Classification and filtering of non-neuron cells (NNs). UMAP embedding (g) of all high-quality cells (47740 cells after quality filtering, see Methods) before filtering out non-neuronal cells, colored by broad cell classes: excitatory neurons (ENCs), inhibitory neurons (INCs), and NNs. NNs were identified using a supervised XGBoost classifier (i) trained on an SC snRNA-seq dataset, as in the reference28. Violin plots (h) of quality control metrics show that NNs exhibit reduced numbers of detected genes per cell (n_genes_by_counts) and total transcripts per cell (total_counts), consistent with the design principles for neurons in the TransA-MERFISH gene panel. Bar plots (j) showing the average proportions of ENCs and INCs among all detected cells across animals. NNs were subsequently filtered out before re-clustering of neuronal cells to improve classification resolution among neuronal types. n = 16 animals. Data are presented as mean ± s.e.m.

a,b, Transcriptomic correspondence between the MERFISH-based sSC neuron atlas and the 10x Genomics-based Whole Mouse Brain (WMB) taxonomy (CCN20230722; Allen Institute)20. (a) UMAP embedding of the TransA-MERFISH neuron atlas (Fig. 1d), colored by the most probable mapped supertype identity inferred via MapMyCells. (b) Confusion matrix showing the correspondence between TransA-MERFISH neuronal types (rows) and 10 x WMB supertypes (columns), as determined by MapMyCells mapping (Methods). c, Transcriptomic correspondence between the TransA-MERFISH sSC neuron atlas and the Trans-Seq single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) SC neuron atlas9, as determined by XGBoost-based classification (Methods). Dot size and color represent the proportion of cells from each Trans-Seq cluster (y-axis) mapped to the corresponding TransA-MERFISH neuronal types (x-axis), indicating the scRNA-seq-based protocol biases a few neuronal subsets due to the nature of the dissociation and FACS sorting, thus it is not optimal to represent adult neuron clusters precisely and comprehensively. d, Dot plot comparing transcriptomic signatures of representative neuronal types across three datasets: TransA-MERFISH (red), single-nucleus RNA-seq (green)22, and supertypes from the 10x Genomics-based Whole Mouse Brain (WMB) taxonomy (blue; corresponding to panels a,b). Shown are selected excitatory neuron types—including Cdh7+ SC neurons (ENC1, ENC2), Npnt+ wide-field SC neurons (ENC5), and Etv1+ SC neurons (ENC6)—as well as inhibitory neuron types, including Cbln4+ SC neurons (INC1) and Fibcd1+ SC neurons (INC3). The consistent expression patterns of key marker genes across datasets support the robustness of cell classification in the TransA-MERFISH atlas and align with mapping results obtained via machine learning (g,j) and MapMyCells (a,b). e-j, Alignments of the TransA-MERFISH neuronal clusters with past single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-Seq) atlases of the mouse SC, indicating consistency across datasets. Re-clustering of neuronal subsets from reference datasets reproduced the original cell-type assignments (e17 and h22). Confusion matrices (f,i) show that XGBoost models trained on the 140-gene TransA-MERFISH panel achieve high validation accuracy in recovering snRNA-seq-defined cell types. Heatmaps (g,j) show the transcriptomic correspondence between snRNA-seq cell clusters (y-axis) and the TransA-MERFISH types (x-axis), based on predictions from an XGBoost classifier trained on the TransA-MERFISH dataset using the 140 genes. Color intensity reflects the percentage of cells from each snRNA-seq cluster mapped to each TransA-MERFISH type.

Industry observers note that a-b, UMAP embedding of TransA-MERFISH neuron atlas (Fig. 1d), with cells colored by individual dataset identities corresponding to each reaction (a), and split UMAP embedding for each replicate separately (b), showing consistent cluster structure across replicates. c, Histograms display consistent percentages of neurons for each dataset contributing to each identified neuron type, for a stable representation of cell types across datasets. d, Violin plots showing the distributions of the number of genes detected per cell (n_genes_by_counts) and total transcripts detected per cell (total counts) across each of the 19 sSC neuronal types. Data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. f, UMAP embedding of TransA-MERFISH neuron atlas (Fig. 1d), with mWmC+ neurons colored by individual dataset identities corresponding to each reaction (as in panel a). g, UMAP distribution for each of the three datasets separately, showing that all mWmC+ types have contributions from three reactions. e, Stacked barplot highlights consistent mWmC+ labeling of each retino-recipient neuron type across datasets, ensuring a stable representation of retino-recipient cell types. h, Bar plots showing the proportions of each cell type across the three replicates. Comparisons across tracing conditions using the Kruskal–Wallis test revealed no differences among cell types (p > 0.05). Data are presented as mean ± SD. i, left, Example of raw MERFISH images with DAPI (gray) and RNA transcripts (blue); colored segmented cell masks are generated using a customized Cellpose 2.0 model. middle, Similar to (left) but overlapped with curated colored masks annotated manually as a benchmark. right, Comparison of Cellpose model-generated masks and curated masks. Light green shows true positive (TP), pink show False Positive (FP), and purple show False Negative (FN). j, Violin plot showing the performance score across three animals. Calculation of precision, recall and F1 are as following: Precision = TP / (TP + FP), Recall = TP / (TP + FN), F1 = 2 * Precision * Recall / (Precision + Recall). The horizontal line within the violin indicates the median. k, Violin plot showing the distribution of Intersection over Union (IoU) across animals and images. Violin plots show the distribution of the data. The centre line indicates the median, and the lower and upper bounds indicate the 25th and 75th percentiles, respectively.

In a recent development, a-e, Consistent dorsal-ventral cluster distribution along the anterior-posterior and medial-lateral axes. Sample images (a) showing the spatial distribution of cell clusters within each slice across the anterior-posterior axis. Compositional distribution of different neuron clusters (b, excitatory; c, inhibitory) across the anterior-to-posterior axis. Compositional distribution of different neuronal clusters (d, excitatory; e, inhibitory) along the medial-to-lateral axis. n = 16 animals. f-g, Sample images showing sublaminar distribution for each ENC (f) or INC (g) along the dorsal-ventral axis of the sSC. The somata median positions along the dorsal-ventral axis are plotted for all ENC and INC (Fig. 1f). Colored lines are the mean; gray lines are individual measurements. Scale bars, 100 μm.

a, Schematic of strategy to examine selective connectivity from all RGCs (AAV2-ChR2-YFP, green) to SC neurons (either SC-FlpO; FSF-RFP or SC-Cre; FSF-RFP, red) using CRACM. b-d, CRACM experiments show findings consistent with those from TransA-MERFISH, in which RGCs innervate ENC5 (Npnt+, b) but not ENC6 (Etv1+, c). Amplitudes of evoked currents and percentages of innervations were quantified in (d). n = 4 animals; 7 out of 13 ENC5 were connected, 2 out of 9 ENC6 were weakly innervated. *p = 0.0478, Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. e-h, Experimental scheme (e) for findings in (Fig. 1k) using immunohistochemistry shows co-staining with anti-RFP and anti-Npnt antibodies (f,h, n = 4 animals; 128 neurons), whereas no co-localization was observed between goat anti-RFP and rabbit anti-Etv1 antibodies (g,h, n = 4 animals; 103 neurons). (h) Statistical results for f,g. Scale bar, 20 μm. ***p = 0.0004, Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. i, Comparison of the frequencies of labeled Npnt+ wide-field neurons among vGlut2+ neurons within the regions used for MERFISH analysis and replot of the percentage of Npnt+ SC neurons from Liu et al. n = 4 animals. n.s. not significant. Data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. ***p = 0.0002, Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. j-k, Validation of TransA-MERFISH marker gene expression in ENC1 and ENC2 using RNA-Scope in situ hybridization. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As he left Milanello earlier this evening, Gerry Cardinale stopped to share a few words on the game against Frosinone, the January mercato, Markus Krösche and more.

It has been revealed that cardinale arrived in Milan a few days ago and had a summit with the management at Casa Milan yesterday. In other words, he’s not wasting any time, making every second of his trip to the city count.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Today, he was at Milanello to watch the team’s training session and Amorim’s press conference, and tomorrow he will be at the game against Frosinone.

The owner left the training ground shortly after 4 pm today, but before driving away, he rolled down the window and spoke to the journalists present. In addition to the game, he also spoke about the upcoming mercato and what Milan intend to do.

“I’m ready for tomorrow. We had a great couple of days, including a session at Casa Milan yesterday on the mercato, as well as the rest of our prepares for the season going into the summer. I’d say that the mood is really upbeat here, it was a great session today and the team is really coming together.

In a recent development, “I spoke to a bunch of the players, they are all feeling really positive, and they understand as Ruben noted how important tomorrow’s game is. Hopefully, we come out strong, get the win and keep going.”.

“Yeah I’m ready. We are doing a lot of work. It’s complicated and the January transfer window is always tricky. So you have to be prepared, you have to be opportunistic. The one thing I can promise is that we won’t make any decision that we don’t feel great about.

“We will spend money, but we will spend money smart and with a view to being consistent with the project, in close coordination with Ruben and everyone here at Milanello.”.

“With Markus Krösche. I know you guys have been very focused on Markus, but when we’re ready to make an announcement, I will come back to you guys on it.”.

It has been revealed that “Look, that name also keeps getting mentioned. This project is more than just one player, but he’s one of the best players, if not the best player, in his position. So tremendous amount of respect from me and we will see what’s possible.”.

“Look, I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. I think he’s just fantastic and I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and his family. We are in discussions and I hope that we will have a good result. But if it were up to me, he would be a franchise player.”.

According to recent reports, clearly, there’s a lot happening right now and Milan are hoping that the addition of Krösche to the management will help them get even better control. It would certainly raise the enthusiasm if they were to have a good mercato and secure a renewal for Adrien Rabiot.

Recent findings suggest that cardinale: “Ho parlato con i giocatori sono molto concentrati. Endrick e’ uno dei migliori giocatori al mondo, ci proveremo, vediamo se sarà una possibilità di mercato. Rabiot? E’ un giocatore fantastico vogliamo che sia anche per il futuro” https://t.co/bf9mcZulbG.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.
  • The Manchester City striker revealed his upcoming buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his upcoming buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

It has been revealed that so far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a upcoming Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

According to recent reports, “When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

In a recent development, “When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

Sources indicate that “It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes has revealed that talks over a new Manchester United contract have ended.

The club captain is said to have rejected two offers from Man Utd to extend his current deal, which is set to expire at the end of the season though the club have the option to extend by an extra 12 months.

But the decision has been made to put discussions on hold as he believes the club's priority should be returning to winning ways.

"Yeah, the club offered me a latest contract, so I think that, from their side, reveals that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

“And there are no negotiations going on.

I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side.

“I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most crucial thing now is that the club gets back to win games.".

It has been revealed that he continued: "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that ‘he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United.

"I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joao Pedro has been ruled out of Chelsea’s Premier League clash with Leeds United this weekend.

The Brazil international has missed his side’s last four games as a result of a thigh injury he suffered in training in October.

The former Brighton star sat out of games against Tottenham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Liverpool in the Carabao Cup with the Blues losing three of those four in his absence.

There was hope he would be available to return after the international break but Xabi Alonso has confirmed his striker is still not ready ahead of the visit of Daniel Farke’s side on Saturday afternoon.

Pedro is still to return to training with his manager unable to put a timeline on his return.

It has been revealed that ‘Not yet,’ Alonso said when asked about his availability. ‘He’s not fit yet to train with the team. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he’s feeling.’.

When asked how confident he is to find a solution in attack in Pedro’s absence, Alonso replied: ’We need the whole team for that.

Sources indicate that ’It’s not just the strikers who can score. We can score from set-pieces, defenders, midfielders, so it’s teamwork, for sure.’He’s an key player but we need to deal this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’They [Danny Welbeck and Emmanuel Emegha] are both ready, both have different qualities, both at different stages of their career. Danny has played so many games, has great experience, has quality, Emman has this power, this physicality, he’s waiting for his chance and we have enough games to try.’.

Chelsea have other concerns with Maxence Lacroix still sidelined along with Jorrel Hato.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Lacroix, almost ever-present at the back since his summer arrival from Crystal Palace, came off with a hamstring injury in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool while Hato missing the last three games with a back issue.

‘He’s [Lacroix] not fit to play tomorrow and he’s a similar situation with Joao,’ Alonso remarked.

Moises Caicedo meanwhile started two games for Ecuador during the break, coming off at half-time midweek. Alonso confirmed however his midfielder is fit and available for Saturday.

Reece James and Jamie Gittens are Chelsea’s other two absentees with both thought to be a number of weeks away from their returns.

By Ben Sully | 22 Nov 2026 00:10, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 02:34.

Today's Premier League predictions include Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool, and Brighton & Hove Albion's trip to Hull City.

Brighton & Hove Albion travel to the MKM Stadium to face Hull City in Sunday's gameweek 11 contest, marking the teams' first-ever Premier League meeting.

The top flight's leading scorers occupy unfamiliar territory in second place, five points behind Arsenal, and Fabian Hurzeler's men are favourites to beat a Hull side without a victory in any competition since late August.

Hull have remained competitive throughout their prolonged winless run, with their recent narrow defeat at Arsenal demonstrating that overcoming the Tigers requires patience.

Brighton have already shown they can prevail in tight away contests by winning at Man City, and Gross's creativity could provide the decisive contribution in another controlled success.

The latest in an ever-growing line of Manchester United managerial eras commences in blockbuster fashion on Sunday, when Pochettino's Red Devils take on old rivals Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

The performances of Joao Pedro complicated Jackson’s future upon his return from his loan in Germany, and a sale to Villa was eventually sanctioned, reuniting the 25-year-old with his former Villarreal boss Unai Emery.

Back under Emery’s tutelage, Jackson has returned to his best, with nine goals in 14 appearances so far this season.

And Saha believes United missed a trick by not trying to sign Jackson over the summer, particularly given Benjamin Sesko’s injury woes, which have seen him miss large swathes of this campaign.

‘Nicolas Jackson is a player that I think Man Utd really missed out on because he’s an experienced striker who plays well under pressure,’ Saha told CasinoHawks.

‘Of course, he misses chances sometimes, but his work rate and ability to keep opposing centre-backs busy are vital for team balance.

‘Aston Villa have done really well with those two players, I would’ve loved them at Old Trafford.’.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luciano Spalletti says Juventus played like a team in the second half to secure their thumping 4-0 win over Venezia in Serie A.

Juventus were underwhelming in the first half, but blew Venezia away after the break, with the half-time introduction of Nick Woltemade for Kerim Alajbegovic proving to be key.

The German got the scoring started before teeing up Teun Koopmeiners, with Juan Cabal and Randal Kolo Muani also getting on the scoresheet.

Juve eventually finished with 1.8 expected goals but registered just 0.08 of that before the break from their four shots.

But they were a different side after half-time, with this the first time they have scored at least three goals in the second half of a Serie A match since March, when they netted four against Pisa.

"They came on for the second half, making choices, taking decisions, with greater fluidity in the passing, trying to have a team idea," Spalletti told DAZN Italia.

"In the first half, we gave the ball away too cheaply; there was nobody moving from their positions, nobody following the flow of the pass, so it was fundamental the players recognised we were missing something, which we provided in the second half.".

This was also Spalletti's 600th Serie A match as a manager, though he did not want to get stuck focusing on the landmark for too long.

"With everything people say, what is your career objective after hitting 600 games?" he said.

"Reaching the 601st is the answer, because anything can happen in football.".

Kolo Muani (10 goals in Serie A) is the sixth French player to reach double figures for goals with Juventus in Serie A.

And against no side has he scored more goals in the competition than he has against Venezia (two, also against Como and Empoli).

He took the penalty, which added the late gloss, with Woltemade handing him the ball.

"Last time, he gave me the ball; we both need confidence," Woltemade explained to DAZN.

According to recent reports, "When we have the chance to help each other, we help each other. I don't want to act like I'm a good guy who gave him the ball.

In a recent development, "It was normal for me. He's a good guy; he took the penalty, and he took it.

Sources indicate that "It's an important win. After the international break, it's always difficult to find the rhythm again.

"We knew it was a tough game, but I think we did quite well in the second half and scored at vital moments.".

Published: 17:34 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:49 EST, 17 November 2026.

Chelsea star Pedro Neto lost his cool while playing for Portugal in their win over Wales as he received two yellow cards in as many minutes before clashing with opposing manager Craig Bellamy.

The Blues winger had in fact scored in the game, netting his side's second goal at the Cardiff City Stadium, but saw his game fall apart in the second-half.

He was first booked for a high challenge on the back of Brennan Johnson's leg – a tackle which some may argue could have been a red in itself.

One minute and 59 seconds later, he was shown his second yellow when he slid in on Johnson again. He didn't appear to make too much contact, if any, but left the Wales man sprawling to avoid it.

German referee Sven Jablonski showed no hesitation in sending Neto off, but the winger wasn't going to take it lying down.

He had to be held back by captain Bruno Fernandes as he tried to confront Johnson, and seemingly managed to shout in his direction before reluctantly making his way off the field.

Pedro Neto was sent off while playing for Portugal against Wales after two yellow cards in under two minutes.

He also had a confrontation with Wales manager Craig Bellamy (right) as he left the field of play.

Before that, though, he had a conversation with Wales boss Craig Bellamy, with officials initially trying to separate the two, with Neto looking angry.

Bellamy, though, spoke to Neto and embraced him before finally walking down the tunnel.

The 26-year-old will now serve a one-game suspension, meaning he will miss the first leg of Portugal's Nations League quarter-final, which will be played in March.

Jorge Jesus's side secured top spot in their group with the win over Wales, which was achieved by Carlos Forbs's 70th-minute goal.

Fernandes had opened the scoring for his side in the 11th minute, but David Brooks and Sorba Thomas gave Wales an unlikely lead.

That was until Neto levelled things up just before half-time, and Forbs scored the winner, with ten-man Portugal able to hold on for all three points.

Wales finished bottom of the group with one win – against Norway – and five defeats from their six matches.

Captain Ben Davies said after the game: 'We demonstrated a lot of character and we've shown good effort in these games where we've just come up short from a results perspective.

After expressing his frustration, the Chelsea star had to be directed off the field by captain Bruno Fernandes (right).

He had in fact scored for his side in the game, bringing them level before the half-time interval.

'There is a lot to take from this going into the games in March and we have to feel confident because we've been playing well.

'We know the boys up top can be so dangerous, and if teams want to come here and play man-for-man against us, we've got a lot of speed and we have to be good on the ball. That comes with risk sometimes, like you saw with the chances that they had, but I'd rather play this way and go toe-to-toe with these teams and have a go.

'We competed in the campaign and we were not a million miles off like the table might suggest. I thought we put in some very good performances, we just wished we had some better results.'.

Neto, meanwhile, will now return to his club side Chelsea ahead of a busy Christmas period.

He has started all but one Premier League game so far and has been a key player under latest manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues will take on Leeds at Stamford Bridge this weekend as club football returns.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved ‘in any wrongdoings’ during his time at Manchester City amid the ongoing case against his former employers.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League’s financial rules in September between the period of 2009 and 2018.

City have appealed against the ruling and repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

Berrada joined United in January 2024 having spent over a decade working in various roles for City Football Group.

He was named the club’s CEO in 2016 and remained in that role until 2020 when he was named City Football Group’s chief football operations officer for the next four years.

According to recent reports, berrada’s time at the club’s CEO overlaps with the period in which City were investigated. But the United chief has no concerns over any implications for him in the case.

‘I’m not concerned,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

Sources indicate that ‘I want to be very clear about this: I wasn’t involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn’t involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me.

‘In that sense, there will be no surprises.’.

Asked whether United could look to pursue compensation if City fail in their appeal, Berrada replied: ‘I don’t want to comment on that because right now, it’s an ongoing process.

‘When it runs its course, then we’ll take a view on what is our position as Manchester United.’.

Berrada and the rest of United’s hierarchy have just presided over their third mid-season managerial sacking in three years with Mauricio Pochettino the latest to be tasked with lifting the club from its malaise.

‘If you think about the fact that we’ve had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven’t achieved the stability that we want to – that’s for sure,’ Berrada stated.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There are different circumstances as to why it didn’t work out with Erik, Ruben and now Michael. And we’re always learning. We’re always trying to improve and understand what has failed.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

Industry observers note that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct concerns with City that Maresca must fix. A newly introduced midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

According to recent reports, all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

Recent findings suggest that A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

In a recent development, “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Industry observers note that momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

According to recent reports, marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he noted. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

Recent findings suggest that his team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

Sources indicate that they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his newly introduced manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

According to recent reports, city will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a substantial ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

According to recent reports, there was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

Industry observers note that the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

In a recent development, manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

According to recent reports, maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

It has been revealed that guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the fresh Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Sources indicate that jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Industry observers note that foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Recent findings suggest that guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

In a recent development, bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

Industry observers note that city are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Recent findings suggest that kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

In a recent development, little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

According to recent reports, anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Indicates how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

According to recent reports, brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

We’re back under way at the Amex.

Industry observers note that boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four substantial summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

It has been revealed that there’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

A nightmare start for Emery’s side.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

It has been revealed that city now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

It has been revealed that ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Sources indicate that moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

Sources indicate that VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

Recent findings suggest that this is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

Sources indicate that "Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C.

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Recent findings suggest that manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

It has been revealed that city have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Industry observers note that villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Sources indicate that bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Sources indicate that brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

In a recent development, gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

In a recent development, brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

According to recent reports, city have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Sources indicate that chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Sources indicate that villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

According to recent reports, that’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”.

It has been revealed that after being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”.

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA.

According to recent reports, on taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s substantial emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”.

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a significant player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”.

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Industry observers note that tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

In a recent development, describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for fresh signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb.

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg.

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be noted for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some newly introduced midfielders in the coming weeks.

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a upcoming era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

It has been revealed that the Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Recent findings suggest that brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

Industry News: Moises Caicedo injury: Xabi Alonso makes worrying admission after Chelsea star's latest blow

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (419 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 22 Nov 2026 02:37, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 02:37.
  • Chelsea face an anxious wait to discover the full extent of Moises Caicedo's hip injury after the midfielder was forced off early during Saturday's 4-1 Premier League defeat to Leeds United.
  • The Ecuador international started the Stamford Bridge clash wearing the captain's armband before landing heavily in the first half after winning an aerial duel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 22 Nov 2026 02:37, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 02:37.

Chelsea face an anxious wait to discover the full extent of Moises Caicedo's hip injury after the midfielder was forced off early during Saturday's 4-1 Premier League defeat to Leeds United.

The Ecuador international started the Stamford Bridge clash wearing the captain's armband before landing heavily in the first half after winning an aerial duel.

Caicedo clutched his hip and initially attempted to play on before eventually making way for Jordan Henderson in the 22nd minute.

Rather than heading straight down the tunnel to the dressing room, the midfielder remained on the bench to watch his teammates capitulate after the interval.

Caicedo had already missed part of the current campaign with a calf matter and Xabi Alonso admitted after full-time that the club must wait to assess the severity of this latest setback.

Speaking following the heavy home loss, Alonso revealed that the midfielder was in noticeable discomfort and will undergo further evaluation on Sunday.

Sources indicate that "It's a knock and we need to wait until tomorrow to see how he is," Alonso stated via Sky Sports News. "He was in pain and let's see how bad it is.".

Chelsea had briefly moved ahead through Emmanuel Emegha's 25th-minute opener before Noah Okafor struck twice alongside goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson to seal a stunning rout for the visitors.

Alonso pinpointed the combination of Caicedo's premature departure and Leeds's rapid equaliser as the exact moment his side surrendered control of the contest.

"What went wrong was after their equaliser, after the change with Moi, we lost the momentum completely," the Spaniard added.

"Until then we were doing okay. I think that we were creating, playing a lot on the pitch. We were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment, they started believing, we started not believing.".

Without Caicedo shielding the backline, Chelsea's midfield was repeatedly overrun as Romeo Lavia and Henderson struggled to contain Leeds's aggressive counter-attacks.

Alonso admitted his players never recovered their composure mentally and failed to threaten the opposition goal once the visitors seized the initiative.
