Industry News: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

📅 30 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.
  • It has been revealed that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five.
  • Recent findings suggest that but perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

It has been revealed that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

Recent findings suggest that but perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso noted. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Industry observers note that jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

It has been revealed that “After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

Recent findings suggest that it is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl.

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Recent findings suggest that neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

Recent findings suggest that “I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

Recent findings suggest that “We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso remarked. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

Chelsea’s newly introduced set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Industry observers note that macPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Industry observers note that fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”.

Industry observers note that palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro notes he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert.

Industry observers note that 6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D.

September 5: Brighton vs Leeds (Premier League)September 13: Coventry vs Brighton (Premier League)September 16: Manchester United vs Brighton (League Cup)September 19: Brighton vs Arsenal (Premier League)October 10: Sunderland vs Brighton (Premier League).

September 6: Arsenal vs Chelsea (Premier League)September 9: Chelsea vs Leeds (League Cup)September 12: Chelsea vs Hull (Premier League)September 18: Brentford vs Chelsea (Premier League)October 10: Chelsea vs Bournemouth (Premier League).

In a recent development, the final game of the day comes from the north west as Manchester United host newly-promoted Ipswich. That game kicks off at 4.30pm and you can follow all the live action from that match right here.

Chelsea 4 Brighton 3 Leeds 1 Brentford 1 Sunderland 1 Fulham 0.

Possession: Chelsea 26%-74% BrightonShots: 17-15Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 4-7Touches in opposition box: 29-28.

Sources indicate that there is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the latest Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

Sources indicate that it could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Absolutely ridiculous decision; there was no foul in any way, shape or form.

According to recent reports, chelsea look to counter through Pedro, who is then brought down by Costinha. It is an easy booking for referee Michael Oliver to give.

How many added minutes will there be? The answer is five minutes.

Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

This is a concern for Chelsea as Caicedo, who came on as a second-half substitute, is now having to go off injured. In his place is former Brighton man Barco, who slapped Bellingham at the World Cup. Barco is booed vociferously by the travelling Brighton fans.

Meanwhile Leeds are level 1-1 against Brentford at Elland Road thanks to Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Brighton scored four a week ago against Aston Villa on the opening weekend but have conceded four this weekend. If they can get a goal though soon, it would make the home fans inside Stamford Bridge very nervous.

Kadioglu has an effort from the edge of the Chelsea box but drags his effort wide.

Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Recent findings suggest that palmer has been pretty quiet today but Chelsea’s two-goal lead is restored. He receives it from Pedro and drives forward through the Brighton half. As he approaches the edge of the penalty area, Palmer calmly slots home into the bottom corner.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel will have like that. He may not have had a brilliant game, but Palmer just scored a brilliant goal. That should be enough for Chelsea.

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:.

Recent findings suggest that #CHEBHAMatch Officials are operating in the second half without communications packs due to an ongoing technical glitch. VAR remains in operation via a back-up system using messages sent to the referee's watch and radio communication to the fourth official if required.

Industry observers note that dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Sources indicate that xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

Industry observers note that this game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a significant deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

In a recent development, england head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

According to recent reports, chelsea have two major chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

According to recent reports, chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea 3 Brighton 1Leeds 0 Brentford 1Sunderland 0 Fulham 0.

Possession: Chelsea 29%-71% BrightonShots: 9-6Shots on target: 4-3Corners: 2-4Touches in opposition box: 15-10.

According to recent reports, chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

Industry observers note that the Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

It has been revealed that there has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

It has been revealed that at 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

Recent findings suggest that the Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Sources indicate that brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their fresh goalkeeper.

Brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler remarked. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

According to recent reports, “We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very key to understand his thoughts but also our planning. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”.

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 10:26.

Liverpool remain the favourites to beat Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League showdown despite the potential for a Mauricio Pochettino upcoming manager bounce, Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Andoni Iraola's side have the honour of hosting Pochettino's Premier League homecoming at Anfield, after Man United dismissed the popular Michael Carrick during the international break.

Pochettino takes over a Man United side who start the day 19th in the Premier League table, 14 places and 10 points worse off than Liverpool, having won just one of their 10 top-flight games this season.

However, Liverpool have only prevailed in one of their five Premier League fixtures at Anfield in 2026-27, while only one of Man United's last nine permanent or interim managers has lost their first game in charge.

Nevertheless, Liverpool Champions League winner Hamann has affirmed that his former side remain the favourites due to one key reason - their more 'settled' squad - but the visit of the Red Devils is still coming at an inopportune time for the Reds.

Industry observers note that “It's certainly not the best time because Man United need a spark from somewhere," Hamann said. They were going through the motions. If you look at Carrick, he's such a lovely guy, but you've got to win games if you're the Man United manager, and I'm not sure whether he believed that his team could turn things around.

In a recent development, "To have a manager on the sideline who comes in and makes everybody think, 'I've got to put my foot down now to keep my place and get in the team', it's certainly not the best time for Liverpool. Whether it's the worst, we'll know after the game or the weekend, but I think it's a great appointment.

It has been revealed that "I always held him in very high regard. What he did at Spurs was exceptional. If you see what happened to Spurs after he left, it really went downhill year by year. It got worse. The fixture is at the wrong time.

"United changed the manager at the wrong time. But it's a challenge, and there are always special games against United. The more settled side at the moment is Liverpool, there's no doubt about it. They go into the game as favourites, but they could have played them at a better time, I think.”.

Sources indicate that pochettino's record against Liverpool does not make for pleasant reading for Man Utd fans, though, as the Argentine has only won three of his previous 19 games vs. the Reds as a manager, suffering 11 defeats.

Comparing Iraola's start to life at Liverpool to Pochettino's statistics from his one year at Chelsea (2023-24), the current Reds boss already holds the edge in a couple of categories across all tournaments.

Pochettino collected 1.75 points per game at Stamford Bridge, while Iraola is right now averaging 1.94 per game with Liverpool, albeit while having taken charge of 35 fewer games.

Iraola's Liverpool also concede at a rate of 1.38 goals per game compared to Chelsea's 1.45 under Pochettino, but the Blues' 2.02 goals per game in 2023-24 marginally betters Liverpool's 2.00 in 2026-27.

Pochettino's Chelsea finished sixth in 2023-24 with 63 points, and at their current rate, Liverpool will trump the Blues' record with 68, as the hosts are averaging 1.8 points per match thus far.

Opinion: Liverpool ready to sign their next Jeremy Jacquet, he's perfect

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The young Frenchman was brought in for around £55 million with plenty of fans, pundits and journalists all saying that Liverpool had spent too much on a player who'd never played outside of France.
  • The fact that he was only 20 years old didn't help matters much either.
  • However, to the surprise of many, he took becoming a Liverpool player in his stride and has arguably been one of their best performers this term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jeremy Jacquet has been a revelation at Liverpool.

The young Frenchman was brought in for around £55 million with plenty of fans, pundits and journalists all saying that Liverpool had spent too much on a player who'd never played outside of France.

The fact that he was only 20 years old didn't help matters much either.

However, to the surprise of many, he took becoming a Liverpool player in his stride and has arguably been one of their best performers this term.

He's far better than Ibrahima Konate ever was and, he's still got another decade left as a top-level player.

So, the fact that Liverpool are ready to sign their next version of him is rather exciting.

Liverpool have entered the transfer race for Giorgio Scalvini.

Liverpool's defence may have had a decent chunk of change spent on it over the last couple of years but, there are still a couple of problem areas that they need to fix.

For example, both Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have massively underperformed this season.

Every time one of them is played, fans want the other to come back in and take their place.

Obviously, this isn't ideal considering Kerkez was expected to be the Reds' next Andy Robertson.

However, the centre of their defence also has a couple of question marks hanging over it thanks to the undecided futures of Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez.

So, Liverpool being linked with Giorgio Scalvini is hardly a surprised, especially with how much potential he has to fulfil.

"Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea are positioning themselves to make a possible move for Atalanta defensive star Giorgio Scalvini, with the highly-rated Italian emerging as a major potential transfer target for 2027, TEAMtalk can exclusively reveal," TEAMtalk wrote.

"TEAMtalk understands that a number of English sides are now carrying out detailed work on Scalvini as the possibility of him finally leaving Atalanta gathers momentum.

"Newcastle United are long-term admirers of the Italy international, but the latest interest is coming from Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea, who have all been monitoring his development.

"United and Liverpool are both assessing their central defensive options as they consider potential reinforcements, with Scalvini increasingly emerging as a player of interest to their recruitment departments.".

Giorgio Scalvini could become Liverpool's next Jeremy Jacquet.

Scalvini has been linked with an exit from Atalanta for a fair few years now.

Ever since he broke into their first team back in the 2021/22 season, the Italian has been of interest to many different clubs around the globe.

However, now that Liverpool have proven that they're giving youngsters a go in their starting XI with their use of Jacquet and others such as Trey Nyoni, they have more ground to stand on than other clubs.

Of course, Scalvini is a tad older than Jacquet at 22 years old but, since they're both young and have a lot of their careers left to go, it's clear to see why the Italian could become Liverpool's next Jacquet.

He also plays as the right-sided centre-back in a back four so, he'd fit straight into Andoni Iraola's plans if they chose to bring him in.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.
  • One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are mentioned to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which reveals his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their newly introduced deals.

In a recent development, alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing matter for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

Industry observers note that it was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

Slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

Sources indicate that he is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

The Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Recent findings suggest that regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

It has been revealed that confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

In a recent development, in the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

In a recent development, in the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

It has been revealed that since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Massive Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a new-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Liverpool need to see more from their big-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

Breaking: Middlesbrough vs Swansea City - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:04.
  • Middlesbrough play host to Swansea City on Tuesday night looking to strengthen their position at the top of the Championship table.
  • Although the Welsh side make the trip to the Riverside Stadium sitting in eighth position, they only trail their next opponents by five points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:04.

Middlesbrough play host to Swansea City on Tuesday night looking to strengthen their position at the top of the Championship table.

Although the Welsh side make the trip to the Riverside Stadium sitting in eighth position, they only trail their next opponents by five points.

After a frustrating end to the fschedule before the November international break, Middlesbrough needed to use the enforced rest to reset and hope for the return of leading marksman Will Lankshear.

Encouragingly for Kim Hellberg, Boro recorded a 2-0 win over Bristol City on Saturday with their star player only being required to play 13 minutes from the substitutes' bench.

Previously, Boro had suffered a 2-0 defeat at Wrexham and were held to a goalless draw at struggling Watford when Lankshear was sidelined through injury.

Despite winning just three of their last six matches, Boro sit in top spot, helped by an eight-game unbeaten run at the Riverside Stadium.

However, Hellberg has witnessed his team concede nine times across those fixtures, something which will only encourage their opponents.

Swansea are still searching for a replacement for Vitor Matos, who has made the decision to leave for Strasbourg.

Club legend Ashley Williams is leading a four-strong interim management team, and it has already been confirmed that they will remain at the helm for this contest.

A 2-2 draw at home to fifth-placed West Bromwich Albion will be viewed as a solid result, particularly when the Baggies missed a penalty in that fixture.

Nevertheless, despite Swansea having the chance to move to within two points of the leaders, they have accumulated just four points from their last six matches.

Furthermore, they are currently on a three-game losing streak on their travels, conceding 10 times in the process.

Middlesbrough Championship form:.

Swansea City Championship form:.

Middlesbrough boss Hellberg must decide whether to hand a recall to Lankshear after he came through his substitute appearance against Bristol City unscathed.

Myles Peart-Harris is an alternative to Riley McGree, but Hellberg may be against making many alterations for this contest.

Alfie Jones and Rokas Pukstas remain on the sidelines through injury.

Williams could decide to freshen up his Swansea XI by introducing Josh Key, Stephen Eustaquio and Zan Vipotnik.

Marko Stamenic continues to serve a three-match ban, while Josh Tymon joins him on the sidelines with a one-game ban for five yellow cards.

Middlesbrough possible starting lineup:.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Arfsten; Berhalter, Morris; Cozier-Duberry, McGree, Conway; Lankshear.

Swansea City possible starting lineup:.

Vigouroux; Lissah, Cabango, Welsh, Key; Just, Fulton, Eustaquio; Yeo, Vipotnik, Eom.

With the current uncertainty at Swansea, they may view this contest as a free hit, essentially leading them to attack for all three points. However, we are backing Boro to record yet another home win and continue to build an advantage at the top of the standings.

Industry News: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

📅 30 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?
  • There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.
  • Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

According to recent reports, in the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “upcoming signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

According to recent reports, ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT.

According to recent reports, defensive rebuilding is next summer’s massive project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

According to recent reports, harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k.

Recent findings suggest that united were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD.

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR.

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

Sources indicate that “There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick mentioned. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

According to recent reports, “It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”.

According to recent reports, there was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that he recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

According to recent reports, asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick noted, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”.

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

Sources indicate that “We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”.

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He highlighted his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a major week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

In a recent development, “There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

In a recent development, “We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”.

Recent findings suggest that speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

Industry observers note that “It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

According to recent reports, “But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

Industry observers note that “We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”.

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx.

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ.

In a recent development, the hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

Sources indicate that “Scoring before half-time is always notable if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”.

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283.

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk.

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV.

Sources indicate that dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

According to recent reports, man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

Industry observers note that the Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR.

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb.

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

According to recent reports, wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k.

In a recent development, some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you….

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa.

In a recent development, enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

Sources indicate that we are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

According to recent reports, ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

In a recent development, end-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

Recent findings suggest that A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD.

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Recent findings suggest that ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT.

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

It has been revealed that davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

Sources indicate that there’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany.
  • They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow.
  • Industry observers note that the scientists see the work as critical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany. Keeping the roots intact, conservationists carefully lift shoots from a donor meadow of seagrass and place them in a bag.

They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow. They've already picked out a prime area for the young plants, which need sandy sediment, shelter from waves and currents and sufficient light and oxygen to thrive.

Industry observers note that the scientists see the work as critical. Myriam Spicka, who heads the NGO Seagrass Conservation, claims she has "seen the changes" in the more than 30 years she's been diving. And she is not the only one who has witnessed the destruction.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Scientists estimate that around 60% of the Baltic coast's seagrass meadows have disappeared.

"That's the bad news," remarked marine ecologist Thorsten Reusch from the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel . "The good news is that the decline has stopped.".

Underwater seagrass meadows feed and shelter fish, crabs, shellfish and many other species. They improve water quality and slow waves, helping protect shores from erosion. And they store carbon in the seabed about 30 to 50 times faster than forests.

Around 70 species of seagrass can be found along the coasts of more than 150 countries. Some grow just below the surface, others at depths of 60 meters or almost 200 feet.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that "Some countries have far more seagrass, particularly in the Indo-Pacific," noted Reusch. "There, it can play a major role in their carbon balance.".

But the value of seagrass goes beyond carbon storage. Its meadows in the Baltic are among the sea's most valuable habitats. They shelter wildlife, stabilize the seabed and act as natural filters by trapping particles and nutrients.

Planting individual seagrass shoots is painstaking work so people like Reinhard Helbig are trying to make it easier.

Through ZosteraTec, the start-up he co-founded, he helps restore marine habitats, including seagrass meadows damaged by offshore activity, such as wind farm construction. His work begins on the beach.

It has been revealed that "Stormy weather helps us. Waves and currents wash seagrass out of the seabed. A day or two later, it washes up here, still fresh," he mentioned.

It has been revealed that the collected shoots are grown and multiplied in ZosteraTec's aquaculture. Several months later, the marine saplings are laid on a plant support. A specially developed machine binds the planted strands with biodegradable thread. The resulting lengths can be laid on the seabed with less diving work.

"We plant here on land to cut down on underwater work. That means fewer dives, and we can do the painstaking work on shore," Helbig stated.

Researchers at the Geomar Helmholtz Center in Kiel are also testing upcoming ways to restore seagrass across larger areas, including using seeds.

Marine ecologist Esther Thomsen reaches into an aquarium tank and pulls out a flowerpot containing seagrass.

It has been revealed that "Ten percent of the plants in our meadows produce seeds. You can clearly see the seeds sitting inside the seed pod," she noted.

Sources indicate that "The big advantage of restoring meadows from seed is greater genetic diversity. And in the future, we should be able to sow seeds over much larger areas," explained Thomsen.

Reusch from Geomar said they currently "think the most promising way to grow meadows that can withstand climate change is to plant individual shoots as a foundation, then sow seeds between them to increase genetic diversity.".

Whether a planting mission is successful is revealed months or even years later.

According to recent reports, thomsen and her colleagues are visiting the first seagrass meadow planted in Germany's Baltic waters in 2021. The divers count shoots, check how densely they grow and record how the meadow has developed.

They then compare it with the donor meadow that supplied the plants. Only that comparison reveals whether the upcoming crop has merely survived or is beginning to function more like a natural one.

"We've just checked the seagrass meadow, and it's really dense. We counted lots of shoots per square," Thomsen mentioned. "It's looking really good.".

This article is based on a Global Us video report.

Ruben Amorim is not a coach who makes a habit of singling out individuals, but he made an exception in Saturday’s press conference.

In a recent development, as MilanNews recall, on the eve of the game against Frosinone, Amorim bluntly admitted that Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot are the ‘irreplaceable’ players in the current squad. Their characteristics and their quality make them unique, in the eyes of the coach and many fans.

It has been revealed that when the American and the Frenchman don’t play, the team’s fluidity and effectiveness suffer significantly. There is a stark contract between Milan when Rabiot and Pulisic play versus when both do not feature.

Amorim’s words were clear in his pre-match presser: “Every player appreciates having the club’s trust. And Pulisic’s fresh contract has helped. When he wasn’t playing, I told you he was still key for Milan, and we can’t forget about the injured players.

“Pulisic is the only player we can’t replace today: the way he moves between the lines, we don’t have another Pulisic. In the last few European matches, we missed him; we had to manage him. If he’s not on the pitch, given his characteristics, you feel it.

It has been revealed that “And you understand how vital he is. He doesn’t talk much, but he speaks a lot on the pitch with his play. He always wants the ball. He and Rabiot always lift the team up. I don’t like to talk about individuals, but I have to.

“I think everyone can understand that. So Pulisic is our present, he will be our future, and I think he has the potential to do even more.”.

Industry observers note that it’s worth noting that the coach emphasised the importance of Pulisic’s contract renewal too. This is also why the club are doing everything possible to reach an agreement for Rabiot.

Cardinale called him a top player and candidly admitted that he adores him, also emphasising how he respects his family. These statements are not coincidental, given that it is his mother who represents the midfielder.

Industry observers note that speaking of which, discussions with Véronique Rabiot are progressing positively. A meeting took place before the derby, which ended with a 3-1 win with a goal for the former Juventus and Marseille midfielder.

In a recent development, the player is happy with the Rossoneri and wants to stay: a definitive agreement on the financial terms needs to be reached. Milan are also willing to adjust the player’s salary in order to secure him for a few more years at Milanello.

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 11:23, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 11:23.

Arsenal backup goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised to make just his second Champions League appearance for the Gunners in Tuesday's league-phase clash with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates.

Mikel Arteta lost David Raya to a shoulder injury in Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw with Newcastle United, although it is still not clear how serious the Spaniard's problem is.

Nevertheless, as Arsenal assess the severity of Raya's injury, Kepa will at least step in here, 10 months after making his UCL debut for Arsenal in January's 3-2 victory over Kairat Almaty.

While Kepa for Raya is an enforced change on Arsenal's end, Arteta could make two more unenforced alterations at the back, swapping out Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori for Ben White and Piero Hincapie respectively.

William Saliba was on the bench for the first time in a Premier League game this season at St James' Park, but as he is still yet to play a single minute of senior football this season, Ezri Konsa should be preferred from the first whistle.

The latter's England teammate Myles Lewis-Skelly can also anticipate a start over Bruno Guimaraes, but there should be no respite for Declan Rice against the current Bundesliga leaders.

The in-form Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze are likely to be retained in attack too, but the more open nature of Champions League games could benefit Viktor Gyokeres over Kai Havertz after the former's goal and assist vs. Slavia Prague, meaning a total of five changes from Arteta.

Bukayo Saka (quad) and Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) remain out for the Premier League champions.

Arsenal possible starting lineup:.

Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres.

Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 90 min read (17972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~90 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1.
  • Solid-organ cancers represent a complex spectrum of pathology, with the intricately associated TME having a pivotal role in disease progression and therapeutic response4,5.
  • Recent findings suggest that previous studies have identified distinct cell subpopulations within the TME based on their gene expression profiles, spatial distributions and functional characteristics17,18,19,20,21.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1. Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope2,3. Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas (tmeatlas.stanford.edu) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

Solid-organ cancers represent a complex spectrum of pathology, with the intricately associated TME having a pivotal role in disease progression and therapeutic response4,5. Within the TME, both stromal and immune cells have emerged as key modulators of tumour growth, invasion and metastasis1,6,7,8,9,10. However, different studies (often in single-organ contexts) have shown conflicting roles for these cells in promoting versus suppressing tumour growth11,12,13,14. The heterogeneity of the TME, both within individual tumours and across tumour types, poses a substantial challenge to understanding the functional diversity of tumour-associated stromal and immune cells3,15,16.

Recent findings suggest that previous studies have identified distinct cell subpopulations within the TME based on their gene expression profiles, spatial distributions and functional characteristics17,18,19,20,21. However, these findings stem largely from isolated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies22,23,24, and subsequent pan-cancer efforts have remained limited in size and scope3,25,26,27,28. To our knowledge, the largest cancer-associated fibroblast atlas to date integrates data from 1,116 samples across 10 tumour types29; the largest tumour endothelial cell atlas includes 575 samples across 19 tumour types30; and no specific tumour mural or nerve atlases have been generated. Pan-cancer immune cell atlases have been larger28, especially those focused on individual immune cell lineages31,32,33; however, these typically have not examined immune cell interactions within the broader TME.

In a recent development, here we integrated single-cell transcriptomic data from 3,381 human and mouse samples across 42 cancer types and 258 datasets to create a definitive TME transcriptional atlas. By mapping this massive cellular landscape, we resolved the stromal and immune ecosystem of solid tumours. Furthermore, by linking enriched subpopulations to poor clinical outcomes, we identified opportunities for future TME-targeted cancer therapies. Key computational predictions are subsequently validated through in vitro and in vivo experiments. Finally, we have consolidated this work into an interactive web atlas (tmeatlas.stanford.edu) and R software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for groups investigating the TME.

Industry observers note that to systematically analyse single-cell transcriptomic data, we evaluated every scRNA-seq cancer study published in the public domain between January 2014 and July 2025. Separate queries were evaluated independently for human and mouse datasets within the foundational public repositories for single-cell transcriptomics: the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and ArrayExpress. We screened a total of 3,975 published datasets (Fig. 1a). Studies specific to either blood or central nervous system cancers were excluded from our analysis, as were those failing to meet specific architectural requirements (Methods; see Fig. 1a,b). Our comprehensive screen identified 190 human and 68 mouse datasets (Supplementary Table 1), collectively comprising more than 15.4 million cells. Collectively, these datasets formed the final analytical cohort, comprising 3,381 individual scRNA-seq samples across 42 unique cancer types (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Tables 2 and 3).

To process the more than 12.8 million human cells from 2,855 samples and 190 datasets (Extended Data Fig. 1a,b and Supplementary Fig. 1), nearly an order of magnitude greater than many recent seminal studies3,25,26,27,28,31,32,33,34, we used sketch-based sampling and memory read optimization (Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). We applied three independent approaches for data integration to reduce batch effects: Harmony, scVI and FastMNN (Extended Data Figs. 1e and 2a). We then projected each integrated result onto the full dataset (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c). Supervised annotation using four methods—canonical marker genes, estimated copy number variation (inferCNV), SingleR and scATOMIC (Extended Data Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. 2)—delineated the presence of seven main cell types across nearly all human cancers (Fig. 2a–c, Extended Data Fig. 1e,f and Supplementary Table 4). These encompass principal stromal (fibroblast, endothelial, mural and nerve) and immune (myeloid and lymphoid) lineages, alongside epithelial cells, which were excluded from subsequent characterization to focus on the two core TME compartments. Comparing the three integration approaches (Supplementary Table 5), Harmony demonstrated the most robust integration and was selected for all subsequent evaluations. The three integration approaches also frequently yielded discordant cell-type assignments for individual cells (Extended Data Fig. 2d–f), highlighting the stochasticity and misclassification risks inherent to relying on any single method35,36. To mitigate this, we provisionally pooled all cells assigned to a specific TME lineage by any of the three algorithms (Extended Data Fig. 1g). Misassigned cells within these overlapping pools were subsequently removed through recursive downstream filtering (Extended Data Fig. 1h and Supplementary Fig. 3a–e), generating final, high-fidelity atlases for the six principal TME cell types (Fig. 2d–i and Extended Data Fig. 1i,j).

It has been revealed that we next characterized cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), the predominant stromal population in the TME37. Following our recursive isolation strategy (Extended Data Fig. 1h), we delineated four transcriptionally distinct CAF meta-clusters (Fig. 2d) expressing canonical markers (PDGFRA, LUM and DCN) and lacking non-fibroblast markers (Extended Data Fig. 4a and Supplementary Fig. 4). Specifically, we identified (1) antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs; class II HLA+), (2) immunomodulatory/inflammatory CAFs (iCAFs; cytokine+), (3) myofibroblastic/mechanoresponsive CAFs (mCAFs; extracellular matrix (ECM)+, mechanotransduction+), and (4) steady-state CAFs (ssCAFs; progenitor-like markers+; Fig. 2d), broadly consistent with observations from our previous work38 and that of others25,39,40,41. High-resolution sub-clustering (Fig. 2d, Supplementary Table 6 and 7 and Supplementary Fig. 4) further stratified these into seven subpopulations: two iCAF (CXCL8+ or ISG15+), two mCAF (LRRC15+ or COL4A1+), two ssCAF (PI16+ or CXCL14+) and one apCAF. All seven subpopulations were conserved across nearly all evaluated tumour types and tissues (Fig. 2d, bottom). Of note, apCAFs were nearly universally present, whereas previous studies had found them only in rare tumour subsets6. Furthermore, the human apCAFs that we identified did not express mesothelial markers such as MSLN, which are characteristic of mouse apCAFs42 (Extended Data Fig. 4a).

Sources indicate that comparing relative abundances between tumour and non-malignant tissues (Fig. 3a), both mCAF populations were significantly enriched in tumours (3.5-fold for LRRC15+; 2.7-fold for COL4A1+; Supplementary Table 8), reflecting cancer-induced desmoplasia37,43. Similarly, iCAFs and apCAFs were enriched in tumour samples (6.3-fold for ISG15+ iCAFs, 1.3-fold for CXCL8+ iCAFs and 2.0-fold for apCAFs), consistent with their roles in inducing immune evasion42 or secreting inflammatory cytokines41. Analysing abundance across tumour stage and patient treatment response, we found ISG15+ iCAFs, LRRC15+ mCAFs and COL4A1+ mCAFs significantly enriched in late-stage (III–IV) versus early-stage (I–II) tumours (1.9-fold, 1.3-fold and 1.2-fold, respectively; Fig. 3b). Treatment responsiveness did not significantly correlate with any CAF subpopulation (Fig. 3c). Overall, ISG15+ iCAFs were the most consistently enriched fibroblast subset defining both the malignant state and advanced disease (Fig. 3a–c, blue box).
